title: bCPAP Project Mentor
description:
JOB TITLE: The bCPAP Project Mentor

TEAM/PROGRAMME: Programme and Operations

LOCATION: Central

GRADE: NAT 4

POST TYPE: National

Safeguarding:

Save the Children does not tolerate any form of exploitation, abuse, or harassment against any person. It is the responsibility of all employees and representatives to protect all people who come in contact with our organization. Save the Children commits to applying the same standards to all its employees and subject them to the same processes regardless of their position, influence, or reputation within or outside of the organization.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

Save the Children International’s Diversity Policy, aims to promote equal opportunity in employment and to ban any kind of discrimination based on sex, age, social class, disability, HIV status, religion, race and ethnicity

INTRODUCTION [PROJECT OVERVIEW]

Save the Children (SCI) is the world’s leading independent non-profit organization for children. Our vision is a world in which every child attains the right to survival, protection, development, and participation. SCI’s Mission is to inspire breakthroughs in the way the world treats children, and to achieve immediate and lasting changes in their lives. In Zambia, Save the Children has been implementing programmes since 1983 across Child Rights Governance, Health and Nutrition, Child Protection, Education, Child Poverty, and Humanitarian Response.

Save the Children, in partnership with Vayu Global Health and the Ministry of Health (MOH), and with funding from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints Charities (LDSC), will implement the Better Care for Small and Sick Newborns in Zambia project. The project aims to reduce facility-level neonatal mortality by improving access to high-quality respiratory care through the implementation of bubble Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (bCPAP), strengthening referral and transfer systems for sick newborns, and enhancing the capacity of health workers across Lusaka, Central, and Southern Provinces. The project will be implemented in ten district-level public health facilities providing maternity services with functional 24-hour inpatient newborn care units. The intervention will strengthen the quality of care for small and sick newborns through evidence-based clinical practice, health systems strengthening, capacity building, mentorship, quality improvement, and sustainable integration of bCPAP services into routine newborn care.

ROLE PURPOSE:

The Better Care for Small and Sick Newborns in Zambia “bCPAP” Project Mentor is responsible for provision of regular on-site clinical mentorship, coaching and quality improvement support to healthcare providers in project - supported health facilities. The role aims to strengthen the capacity of healthcare providers to deliver evidence-based newborn care, improve adherence to national clinical standards and protocols, and enhance the quality of care for small and sick newborns, contributing to improved neonatal survival and long-term health outcomes.

Working closely with facility-based healthcare teams, Provincial and District Health Offices, and the Ministry of Health, the Project Mentor will build the clinical competencies and confidence of frontline providers in the use of bubble Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (bCPAP), newborn stabilization, infection prevention and control, referral and transfer of sick newborns, and other essential newborn care interventions. The role will promote continuous learning, problem-solving, and quality improvement to institutionalize best practices and strengthen routine newborn care services.

The bCPAP mentor works closely with the project manager, MEAL officer and other functions within the country office including the Health and Nutrition technical lead to meet all program-related objectives in line with the project and Country Office strategy. She/He is accountable for effective and efficient capacity strengthening and evidence-based practice standardisation for the “Better Care for Small and Sick Newborns in Zambia” project across all provinces and facilities with focus on appropriate quality newborn care service delivery.

This project aligns with the Zambia National Health Strategic Plan (2022–2026), particularly its priorities of achieving measurable reductions in neonatal mortality and morbidity through improved quality newborn care anchored on strategic planning, implementation and proactive coordination. The Project Manager will ensure delivery of high-quality, evidence-based interventions such as CPAP while strengthening Ministry of Health systems, building sustainable local capacity, and ensuring compliance with donor and organizational requirements. By strengthening systems for quality service delivery, maintenance, and monitoring of CPAP services, the program will support national newborn health goals and position the intervention for government‑led scale‑up if successful.

Role Dimensions:

Project mentor has overall accountability for all capacity strengthening activities for the project ranging from organizing and spearheading offsite Trainer of Trainer sessions for newborn trainings and cascade of Low-Dose, High-Frequency (LDHF) training sessions, well planned regular mentorships and supporting the initiation and monitoring of district and facility level Quality Improvement (QI) initiatives. The job holder manages some key and strategic communications with all provincials, district and facility level leadership during their operations in consultation with the project manager. The role provides ongoing technical support to healthcare providers to ensure adherence to national clinical guidelines, evidence-based newborn care practices, and the appropriate use and maintenance of bubble Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (bCPAP) equipment. The Project Mentor also supports health facilities to identify service delivery gaps, implement quality improvement actions, monitor progress, and promote the use of routine data for continuous learning and decision-making.

Working under the overall leadership of the Project Manager, the Project Mentor maintains regular engagement with the Ministry of Health, Provincial Health Offices, District Health Offices, and health facility management teams to coordinate mentorship activities and strengthen local ownership of project interventions. The position represents the project during technical meetings, training sessions, mentorship visits, and other implementation activities as delegated by the Project Manager.

The Project Mentor works collaboratively with the Health and Nutrition Technical Lead, MEAL Coordinator, Finance, Supply Chain, Human Resources, Awards, and other Country Office support functions to ensure effective planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of project activities. The role also contributes to documenting lessons learned, identifying implementation challenges and opportunities, and promoting adaptive management to ensure high-quality programme delivery and sustainable improvements in newborn care.

SCOPE OF ROLE:

Reports to: Project Manager

Staff reporting to this post: (0)

Indirect:

Budget Responsibilities: Shall hold activity-based budgets under the supervision of the project manager

KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:

1.Technical/Clinical Leadership

  • Lead knowledge strengthening efforts through clinical competencies, confidence, and performance of healthcare providers delivering care to small and sick newborns through structured mentorship, coaching, supportive supervision, quality improvement initiatives, and continuous skills reinforcement
  • Drive sustainable improvements in newborn survival by embedding evidence-based clinical practices into routine service delivery while strengthening local ownership and facility-based capacity through onsite LDHF
  • With support from the province, districts and facility groomed newborn champions provide regular on-site mentorship to healthcare workers in: Essential Newborn Care, Small and Sick Newborn Care, advanced newborn care, respiratory distress management including initiation and care on bCPAP
  • Support initiation and implementation of QI initiatives and committees for sustainable quality newborn service delivery such as Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) and Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) to foster low-cost high impact interventions that support newborn survival
  • Support monitoring of all implementation activities including neonatal equipment availability, maintenance (working closely with facility biomedical technicians), safe and appropriate use based on the standards to foster alignment between project operations and strategic goal
  • Support facilities to strengthen clinical documentation, case management, adherence to service delivery guideline and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP’s) including those related to the up-to-date newborn district referral systems, clinical audits related to performance, perinatal mortality reviews and infection prevention standards.
  • Ensure integration of gender equality, safeguarding, disability inclusion and child rights throughout implementation.
  • Working with the MEAL officer, support health workers to improve documentation quality, interpret routine health data, monitor newborn outcomes, and use data proactively to inform newborn care quality improvement initiatives.

2. Program Planning and implementation Support

Support implementation of all project capacity strengthening components including:

  • Support with expertise rigorous application of Social and Behaviour Change Communication theory, practice, principles and current best practices with capacity to achieve measurable results for the sick newborns across all implementing facilities
  • Keep updated a repository of all capacity building activities including input, process and output resources that can be used for project specific and organisational shared learning.
  • Support implementation of competency-based capacity strengthening strategies such as overseeing Training of Trainers (TOT) implementation model with cascaded onsite Low Dose High Frequency (LDHF) and mentorships for assured systems strengthen long-term institutional capacity.
  • Promote leadership development among facility champions to foster appropriate and sustainable evidence-based QI initiatives through functional facility QI teams
  • Proactively participate in planning and conducting of the project baseline and facility readiness assessments, capacity strengthening and procurement planning needs for effective onsite clinical oversight

3. Stakeholder Management

Develop and maintain strong working relationships with stakeholders by:

  • Working with MOH mentors across all levels and taking responsibility to ensure alignment government set standards for newborn practice for easy project integration and sustainability beyond active implementation
  • Work with Vayu Global Health technical advisors to align with national standards related to the use of bCPAP equipment
  • Work and collaborate with Pediatric Association of Zambia (PAZ), relevant academic institutions and Church volunteer clinicians to support training and mentorship activities and foster high-quality implementation of newborn interventionswith
  • Work with relevant program staff to ensure all implementing partners undergo legal vetting and capacity assessment prior to commencing work with Save the Children.
  • Ensure that all partners are engaged with appropriate agreements and effective monitoring systems are in place so that partner delivery meets donor expectations and requirements
  • Represent Save the Children during technical working groups, steering committees and coordination meetings with full recognition of The Christ of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints contribution to the project

4. Documentation and Program Reporting.

The project mentor will:

  • Ensure monthly mentorship reports, action plans and Quality Improvement updates to monitor health care worker competencies in newborn care, isolate gaps easily and design mitigation measures
  • Conduct competency assessment reports based on clinical practice and LDHF sessions to foster increased adherence to national newborn care guidelines
  • Support correct documentation of success stories, lessons learnt and provide timely feedback to project management.
  • Ensure timely submission of high-quality monthly mentorship and all other capacity strengthening related progress reports in accordance with the project reporting schedule and formats/guidelines

5. Advocacy, Networking and influencing

  • Support district and facility level advocacy for children and other vulnerable groups in the Impact Area based on SCI guidelines and standards
  • Builds strategic networks, coalitions and alliances on project related key advocacy issues with relevant health facility teams
  • Ensure Advocacy for children is integrated in programme and project operations and plans.
  • Document lessons and learning’s from advocacy engagements in synch with the MEAL officer under project manager’s oversight
  • Work closely with partners in the districts to foster synergy and visibility for the organisation including attending key and agreed upon district and Sub- national meetings for purpose of advocacy.
  • Work with Child Safeguarding Focal persons to ensure all CO staff are trained in CS
  • Closely review documents and agreements to ensure all partners, contractors, visitors, volunteers etc. comply with CS and code of conduct standards

6 Child Safeguarding

  • Work with Child Safeguarding Focal persons to ensure all CO staff are trained in CS
  • Closely review documents and agreements to ensure all partners, contractors, visitors, volunteers etc. comply with CS and code of conduct standards

SKILLS AND BEHAVIOURS (our Values in Practice)

BEHAVIOURS (Values in Practice)

Accountability:

  • Holds self-accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values
  • Holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities - giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved.

Ambition:

  • Sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages their team to do the same

Previous working relationships within donor funded programs and with key multilateral agencies, and bilateral donors;

title: Scrum Master, Lion Holdings
description:

title: Product Development Engineer II
description:
The Opportunity:

This position is a focused, technical engineering role responsible for supporting and helping to drive technical product innovation and the development of creative new product concepts into manufacturable solutions. This position also provides project support to more senior engineers acting as mentors to help gain experience. This position serves as focal point for driving technical engineering solutions on new product concepts to ensure financial targets, schedule, and adherence to specified safety and quality standards. The position also drives Brand level value engineering and advanced product quality planning. The job role serves as a technical engineering liaison with Operations and collaborates with the cross functional New Product Development Team to support efficient flow of new product concepts through the new product development lifecycles.   • Awareness to toy industry norms and regulation (ASTM and ISO)

title: Software Developer 4
description:
Job Description

Join OCI’s Edge Security team as a Principal Software Engineer focused on building and scaling Oracle Cloud Infrastructure’s Web Application Firewall (WAF) platform. You will lead the design and development of highly available, cloud-scale services that protect customer applications from web-based threats, automate security enforcement, and deliver advanced traffic inspection and policy management capabilities across OCI’s global infrastructure.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the architecture and delivery of cloud-scale backend services that power OCI’s Web Application Firewall (WAF), API Security, and application protection capabilities.
  • Design and evolve scalable policy management, rule evaluation, threat detection, bot mitigation, traffic inspection, and security analytics platforms with focus on reliability, performance, and extensibility.
  • Build highly available distributed systems that inspect and process large volumes of HTTP/HTTPS traffic while maintaining low latency and a seamless customer experience.
  • Drive the technical strategy for application security services, partnering with Security Engineering, Product Management, Edge Infrastructure, and Platform teams to deliver new capabilities.
  • Establish operational excellence through SLOs/SLAs, incident response processes, runbooks, root‑cause analysis, and continuous service improvement.
  • Lead automation initiatives across the software development lifecycle, including CI/CD pipelines, testing frameworks, deployment automation, Infrastructure‑as‑Code, and developer productivity tooling.
  • Mentor engineers, influence technical strategy across organizations, and raise the engineering bar through design reviews and technical leadership.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead the architecture and delivery of cloud-scale backend services that power OCI’s Web Application Firewall (WAF) platform.
  • Design and evolve highly available policy management, rule evaluation, traffic inspection, bot mitigation, API protection, and security analytics services.
  • Build scalable distributed systems that process and analyze high volumes of HTTP/HTTPS traffic while maintaining low latency and high reliability.
  • Drive engineering excellence through software architecture reviews, design documentation, code quality standards, and operational best practices.
  • Partner closely with Security Engineering, Product Management, SRE, and OCI platform teams to define and deliver next‑generation application security capabilities.
  • Establish robust observability through metrics, logging, tracing, alerting, and performance monitoring to ensure service health and customer visibility.
  • Lead automation initiatives across the software development lifecycle, including CI/CD, testing frameworks, deployment automation, and Infrastructure‑as‑Code.
  • Drive reliability, scalability, and operational readiness through capacity planning, incident response, root‑cause analysis, and continuous improvement.

How You’ll Have Impact

  • Deliver core WAF capabilities that protect OCI customers from application‑layer attacks while maintaining performance and availability.
  • Launch customer‑facing security features that provide visibility, protection, automation, and policy control at cloud scale.
  • Improve the scalability, reliability, and operational maturity of OCI’s application security platform.
  • Raise engineering quality and technical standards through mentorship, architectural leadership, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Ways of Working

  • Security, privacy, and reliability by design with secure development practices embedded throughout the software lifecycle.
  • Data‑driven decision making supported by clear metrics, SLOs, operational reviews, and measurable customer outcomes.
  • Collaborative engineering culture focused on design reviews, code reviews, technical excellence, knowledge sharing, and continuous learning.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building or operating Web Application Firewall (WAF), API Security, Bot Management, CDN, Edge Computing, or related security products.
  • Knowledge of common web application attack vectors, including OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, credential abuse, automated attacks, and API threats.
  • Experience with rule engines, policy evaluation systems, threat detection platforms, or traffic inspection technologies.
  • Background building high‑throughput analytics, telemetry, or event‑processing pipelines for real‑time security insights.
  • Experience operating globally distributed services across multiple regions and availability domains.
  • Familiarity with modern security architectures, Zero Trust principles, identity and access management, and secure service‑to‑service communication.
  • Experience with compliance, audit readiness, and security‑by‑design development practices.
  • Contributions to open‑source software, security tooling, or cloud infrastructure projects.

Qualifications

  • 7–10+ years building production software systems, including experience developing large‑scale distributed services in cloud or SaaS environments.
  • Strong proficiency in one or more of the following languages: Java, Go, Python, C++, or Rust.
  • Deep expertise in distributed systems design, including scalability, resiliency, concurrency, fault tolerance, service communication, and API design.
  • Strong understanding of HTTP/HTTPS, REST APIs, TLS, reverse proxies, caching, load balancing, and web application architectures.
  • Experience building customer‑facing platform services with strict requirements around availability, performance, and operational excellence.
  • Proven experience with cloud‑native technologies, including containers, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, Infrastructure‑as‑Code, and automated testing frameworks.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals, including design patterns, performance optimization, code quality, and secure software development practices.
  • Experience building observability solutions using metrics, distributed tracing, centralized logging, dashboards, and alerting systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical initiatives and influence architecture decisions across multiple engineering teams.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills with a track record of working effectively across engineering, security, product, and operations organizations.

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance, including expert medical opinion
  • Short‑term disability and long‑term disability
  • Life insurance and AD&D
  • Supplemental life insurance (Employee/Spouse/Child)
  • Health care and dependent care Flexible Spending Accounts
  • Pre‑tax commuter and parking benefits
  • 401(k) Savings and Investment Plan with company match
  • Paid time off, flexible vacation for salaried positions, accrued vacation for other employees

  • Paid sick leave: 72 hours upon hire, refreshed annually

title: Senior Buyer
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Anduril Imaging team develops state-of-the-art imaging systems across both hardware and software, deployed to tackle the most significant security challenges of America and its allies. The team is heavily involved in utilizing computer vision, perception, electro-optical, infrared, and sensor data to give the US and its allies an advantage.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a member of the Supply Chain Team, you will be responsible for managing supplier relationships, negotiating prices, and ensuring parts are delivered on time. This is an exciting opportunity to be apart a growing and dynamic team working closely with engineering and manufacturing teams to support the development and sourcing of cutting-edge defense technologies. The right person for this role is someone who can excel in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment where small teams share a broad variety of duties; has strong people and communication skills; is eager to identify opportunities, find solutions, execute plans, and evaluate results critically and expediently; is committed to learning from mistakes and driven to improve and enhance performance of oneself, others, and the company.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own procurement process cradle-to-grave for multiple product lines or commodity types
  • Lead cross-functional projects to achieve cost, quality, and delivery targets
  • Maintain procurement master data across multiple Bill of Materials to ensure accurate information is flowed to Planning and Production
  • Support Sourcing Engineering & Manufacturing teams to determine best sources
  • Identify and execute cost reduction projects; including strategic procurement and commercial term negotiation
  • Onboard new suppliers in accordance with Anduril Quality Manual and maintain the Approved Supplier List
  • Evaluate suppliers using procurement KPIs and analyze performance trends as part of the Supply Chain performance reviews
  • Conduct research, benchmark, and collect market data to ensure a best-in-class supply base
  • Place purchase orders and resolve downstream issues with receiving, finance, and accounting

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8+ years of Procurement or Supply Chain Management experience
  • A bachelors degree or equivalent experience
  • Experience with ERP and PLM systems
  • Experience with technical procurement

title: Senior Advisor for National and Regional Initiatives
description:
The Senior Advisor for National and Regional Initiatives serves as a strategic advisor to the Science, Energy, and Innovation Directorate (SEI) Associate Laboratory Director on the development of initiatives that strengthen Savannah River National Laboratory’s (SRNL) role within the nation’s research, engineering, manufacturing, and innovation ecosystem.

Through engagement with government, industry, academia, national laboratories, and regional partners, the Senior Advisor identifies emerging opportunities, develops collaborative initiatives, and builds innovation ecosystems that position SRNL to address evolving national and regional priorities.

Working across SEI and the broader research enterprise, the Senior Advisor connects SRNL’s scientific, engineering, and manufacturing capabilities with strategic partners to develop initiatives that expand the laboratory’s impact and strengthen its long-term strategic position.

The position complements the responsibilities of Portfolio Directors, the Technology Partnerships Office (TPO), the Advanced Manufacturing Collaborative (AMC), and the research divisions by developing strategic initiatives that are ultimately transitioned to those organizations for execution and long-term stewardship. The Senior Advisor serves as an institutional integrator—connecting people, organizations, and capabilities to create opportunities that no single organization could develop independently.

The Senior Advisor succeeds by creating strategic opportunities that no single organization within SEI could develop independently and by transitioning those opportunities into sustained laboratory capabilities through collaboration with Portfolio Directors, TPO, AMC, and the research divisions.

Strategic Positioning

  • Assess emerging national and regional science, technology, manufacturing, and energy priorities to identify opportunities where SRNL can provide unique leadership.
  • Develop and advance initiatives that position SRNL as a preferred partner in strategically important mission areas.
  • Represent SEI in forums that influence future science, engineering, manufacturing, and innovation priorities.
  • Strengthen SRNL’s visibility and reputation as a trusted national laboratory partner

Strategic Engagement

  • Build enduring relationships with senior leaders across government, industry, academia, national laboratories, and regional organizations.
  • Convene stakeholders to shape collaborative responses to emerging national and regional priorities.
  • Expand SRNL’s network of strategic collaborators and institutional partners.
  • Foster long-term relationships that create future opportunities for research, engineering, manufacturing, and innovation.

Ecosystem Development

  • Design and develop regional and national innovation ecosystems aligned with SRNL’s strategic priorities.
  • Build collaborative models that integrate research organizations, industry, manufacturing partners, universities, government, and other stakeholders.
  • Develop concepts for public-private partnerships, research consortia, shared infrastructure, workforce collaborations, and multi-institution initiatives.
  • Identify opportunities to leverage federal, state, and private-sector investments that strengthen SRNL’s strategic position.

Initiative Development

  • Conceive and develop strategic initiatives that address emerging national and regional priorities.
  • Identify opportunities that span multiple portfolios, technical disciplines, and organizational boundaries.
  • Build coalitions of government, industry, academia, and laboratory partners around shared objectives.
  • Identify and cultivate prospective partners before formal funding opportunities emerge.
  • Develop governance models, partnership strategies, funding approaches, and implementation roadmaps.
  • Coordinate cross-organizational planning to align scientific capabilities with institutional opportunities.
  • Mature initiatives until they are ready for operational execution by the appropriate Portfolio Director, TPO, AMC, or research division.

Strategic Leadership

  • Serve as a strategic advisor to the Associate Laboratory Director on initiatives that advance SEI’s long-term objectives.
  • Provide strategic counsel on emerging national priorities, institutional partnerships, and collaborative opportunities.
  • Promote collaborative approaches that strengthen institutional partnerships across organizational boundaries.
  • Represent SRNL in executive-level engagements with government, industry, academia, national laboratories, and regional organizations.
  • Champion collaborative approaches that strengthen the national research and innovation ecosystem.

Organizational Interfaces

The Senior Advisor is responsible for the development, integration, and institutional design of strategic initiatives. Once an initiative reaches execution readiness, lead responsibility transitions to the appropriate line organization.

  • Portfolio Directors assume responsibility for sponsor engagement, portfolio strategy, and technical execution.
  • Technology Partnerships Office (TPO) assumes responsibility for partnership agreements, CRADAs, licenses, and related partnership mechanisms.
  • Advanced Manufacturing Collaborative (AMC) assumes responsibility for manufacturing strategy, engineering implementation, demonstration, and scale-up activities.
  • Research Divisions assume responsibility for sustained scientific and technical execution.

Following transition, the appropriate line organization is accountable for execution, while the Senior Advisor continues to provide strategic alignment and institutional coordination, as appropriate.

Success Measures

Success will be evaluated through outcomes such as:

  • 2–3 strategic national or regional initiatives advanced under the Senior Advisor’s leadership that reached execution readiness and were adopted by a Portfolio Director, TPO, AMC, or research division.
  • Growth in non-federal cost-share and partner investment associated with initiatives the Senior Advisor helped shape, in collaboration with the executing organization.
  • The Associate Laboratory Director’s assessment of the Senior Advisor’s strategic counsel on emerging national and regional priorities, institutional positioning, and collaborative opportunities.
  • Effective coordination with Portfolio Directors, TPO, AMC, and research divisions, demonstrated through clearly understood organizational roles and positive stakeholder feedback.
  • Increased participation and leadership in emerging DOE and other federal priority areas.
  • Development of regional and national innovation ecosystems that strengthen SRNL’s strategic position.

Required

  • Advanced degree in engineering, science, public policy, business, or a related discipline.
  • Demonstrated success developing and leading complex multidisciplinary initiatives involving multiple organizations.
  • Experience working with Federal R&D organizations, national laboratories, or comparable innovation ecosystems.
  • Strong understanding of the national laboratory environment and the federal research enterprise.
  • Proven ability to influence across organizations without relying on formal authority.
  • Exceptional communication, relationship-building, strategic planning, and organizational leadership skills.

Preferred

Experience in one or more of the following:

  • DOE national laboratories
  • Federal R&D policy and programs
  • Public-private partnerships
  • Consortium development
  • Regional innovation ecosystems
  • Advanced manufacturing
  • Research infrastructure
  • Technology transition
  • Industry collaboration

Desired Characteristics

The successful candidate will:

  • Think institutionally rather than organizationally.
  • Build institutions, not just initiatives—creating enduring partnerships, collaborative ecosystems, and strategic capabilities that strengthen SRNL’s long-term national impact.
  • Connect technical excellence with national priorities.
  • Build coalitions that span organizational and institutional boundaries.
  • Recognize emerging opportunities before formal funding opportunities are announced.
  • Create collaborative structures that outlast individual projects.
  • Operate comfortably at the intersection of science, engineering, manufacturing, policy, and innovation.
  • Inspire collaboration through influence rather than formal authority.

title: Intermediate Geotechnical Engineer
description:
Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.

We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.

Role description:

We are seeking an Intermediate Geotechnical Engineer to join our growing Geotechnics team in Western Canada (based in Vancouver). In this role you will work under the direction of senior technical leads and project managers, contributing to the investigation, analysis, design and delivery of multi-discipline infrastructure projects spanning roads, transit, ports and marine sectors. You will gain exposure to large-scale assignments while learning and advancing your technical and consulting capabilities.

This role offers the chance to work with a high-performing team, mentor junior staff, build strong client relationships and leverage Arcadis’s national and global resources and expertise.

Role accountabilities:

In this role, you will assist in planning and executing geotechnical site investigations, overseeing activities such as mobilization, field data collection, subcontractor coordination, and diligent logging of geotechnical data. You will be responsible for conducting engineering analyses and design work under supervision, supporting a range of projects involving foundation systems, retaining structures, slopes and embankments, excavations and tunnels, as well as ground improvement measures.

You will interpret soil, rock, and groundwater conditions, leveraging your findings to produce reliable geotechnical recommendations and parameters that inform both design and construction phases. Additionally, you will prepare and review a variety of technical deliverables, including geotechnical interpretative reports, design reports, technical memoranda, calculations, drawings, and cost estimates. Providing construction support services will also be a key aspect of the role, requiring you to review contractor submissions, conduct site observations, assess changed conditions, and collaborate closely with construction teams and clients.

Participation in multi-discipline project teams will be an important part of your responsibilities, where you will help support scope, schedule, and budget activities, and coordinate effectively with other engineering disciplines and internal teams. You will contribute to client engagements by assisting in proposal development, work-planning, budgeting, and preparing submission materials to ensure successful project delivery.

Furthermore, in this role you will support mentoring and knowledge sharing with junior engineers and technologists, encouraging technical growth and fostering a collaborative learning environment. You will be expected to stay current with industry best practices, emerging technologies, relevant codes, and digital delivery methods, actively contributing to process improvements within the Geotechnics practice.

Qualifications & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Geotechnical, Civil or Geological Engineering; a Master’s degree in geotechnical engineering or related discipline is an asset
  • Eligible for registration as a Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) in British Columbia (or already registered) or willing to pursue registration
  • Typically 3-8 years of progressive experience in geotechnical engineering consultancy or infrastructure design and delivery, with some exposure to transportation, transit, ports/marine or heavy civil sectors
  • Experience interpreting geotechnical investigations and preparing geotechnical interpretative reports and design reports
  • Knowledge of geotechnical design of foundations, retaining structures, slopes, earthworks and ground improvement; familiarity with seismic, liquefaction or numerical modelling is an asset
  • Proficiency with geotechnical and design software (for example: GeoStudio Suite, PLAXIS, Slide, CPeTiT, CLiq, LiqSV, Settle3, LPile / APile / RS Pile or equivalent), and with technical report writing
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with ability to convey technical findings clearly; excellent interpersonal, problem-solving and collaborative skills
  • A positive and proactive attitude with the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a multi-discipline team, manage multiple tasks and learn new technical domains
  • Valid driver’s licence and willingness to travel to sites within Western Canada as required

Why Arcadis?

We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It’s why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.

You’ll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you’ll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.

Together, we can create a lasting legacy.

Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging

We want you to be able to bring your best self to work every day which is why we take equality and inclusion seriously and hold ourselves to account for our actions. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice and provide a great place to work for all our people. We are an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. Women, minorities, people with disabilities and veterans are strongly encouraged to apply. We are dedicated to a policy of non-discrimination in employment on any basis including race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, disability, veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

title: Senior Director, Oncology Small Molecule
description:
Job Description

Discovery Oncology is seeking a visionary and strategic leader to shape and drive the discovery and advancement of the next generation of our Company's Oncology small molecule therapeutics. Come join an incredible team steeped in a history of scientific excellence and successful drug discovery.

The successful candidate will lead a team at our company's Boston site delivering on the small molecule Oncology pipeline. They will be the strategic leader for Oncology small molecule therapeutics in Boston, with opportunities to contribute across additional modalities. They will develop and execute a comprehensive pipeline strategy, partnering across our company to expand our portfolio. This leader will work tightly with chemistry, clinical, translational, and business development to build and progress an effective pipeline of compelling medicines, from discovery through late-stage development. The successful candidate will have a strong record of scientific excellence, thoughtful strategic planning, late-stage research and IND experience, and inspiring people leadership.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute a forward-thinking pipeline strategy, shaping the future of our Company's Oncology therapeutics with a focus on small molecules.

  • Be a strategic thought leader for the employment of small molecules to create effective, tolerable, and combinable medicines that are both first-in-class and best-in-class.

  • Leverage your deep understanding of cancer biology (including intrinsic pathways and key cancer drivers) and the current internal and external oncology landscape to evaluate the opportunity of new therapeutics and drive portfolio decisions.

  • Provide strategic oversight for programs as they transition from early discovery into and through late-stage clinical development, ensuring continuity and alignment with the overall asset strategy.

  • Drive key milestones for pipeline advancement, from preclinical candidate selection through to IND-enabling studies and support for early clinical development. Ensure compelling engagement with regulatory agencies.

  • Lead business development evaluations from a scientific perspective, identifying and championing external assets and platforms that align with our strategic vision.

  • As a member of the Discovery Oncology Leadership team, meaningfully contribute to the development and execution of strategy and the growth and development of staff. Act as an experienced Program Lead and mentor others to become strong Program Leaders.

  • Foster a high-performance culture of collaboration, engagement, self-accountability, and inclusion. Establish strong relationships within highly collaborative, multidisciplinary teams to effectively drive drug discovery initiatives.

Required Qualifications / Education:

  • Ph.D. in Biology, Oncology, Pharmacology, Biochemistry, Toxicology, Biophysics, Immunology, or a related STEM subject area with 10+ years of post-degree experience in industry or equivalent.

  • An extensive background in cancer biology with a proven ability to translate deep scientific insights into drug development strategies from discovery through late-stage development.

  • Evidence of innovative approaches to small molecule design, particularly induced proximity.

  • A proven track record of successfully advancing multiple well-designed investigative small molecule drug candidates into the clinic, with a focus on patient experience and successful clinical execution.

  • Clear experience in late program leadership partnering with regulatory, translational sciences, and clinical development. Direct, hands-on experience writing IND modules and filings.

  • Experience managing a group of senior and junior scientists with a track record of achievements, including project leadership and strategic contributions.

  • Ability to build strong relationships within highly collaborative, multidisciplinary teams to effectively drive drug discovery initiatives.

  • Excellent attention to detail and strong communication (oral and written) skills.

  • Highly self-motivated and capable of prioritizing deliverables.

Preferred Experience and Skills:

  • Preference will be given to candidates with a large breadth of small molecule experience, including novel approaches.

  • Experience with modalities beyond traditional small molecules is beneficial, particularly including small molecule payloads.

Cancer Research, Drug Development, External Collaboration, High Performance Team Building, Immunotherapy, IND Submission, Innovation, Investigational New Drug (IND), Motivation Management, Multidisciplinary Collaboration, Oncology, People Leadership, Program Leadership, Project Leadership, Small Molecules, Strategic Management, Strategic Planning

Program & Project Leadership

  • Manage project scope, timelines, budgets, and stakeholder expectations across regions and functions.
  • Drive disciplined program management by implementing best-in-class project management methodologies, governance frameworks, and performance tracking mechanisms.
  • Provide technical leadership and strategic direction for program delivery at a regional level, supporting consistency, scalability, and execution excellence across markets.
  • Contribute to the continuous evolution of program management approaches, tools, and methodologies to drive innovation, efficiency, and differentiation within GBS.

Stakeholder Management

  • Partner with business stakeholders, functional heads, and regional delivery teams to define project objectives, success metrics, and adoption of GBS-led initiatives/programs.
  • Communicate project progress, risks, and dependencies through structured updates, business reviews and program dashboards.
  • Facilitate alignment across time zones, cultures, and business units to achieve common goals.
  • Build and sustain strong executive‑level relationships to enable effective decision‑making, issue escalation, and timely resolution of complex program challenges.
  • Align diverse stakeholder interests across regions, functions, and delivery partners to ensure shared ownership of outcomes and benefits realization.

Change & Transformation

  • Lead the change management strategy for programs, ensuring people, process, and technology impacts are understood and addressed.
  • Oversee communication plans, training needs, and adoption activities to enable smooth implementation and sustained business readiness.

Governance & Compliance

  • Ensure projects comply with corporate governance, risk management, and compliance frameworks.
  • Establish and maintain program governance structures, including steering committees, working groups, risk reviews, and milestone gating.
  • Maintain high standards of documentation, project tracking, and reporting to ensure transparency and accountability. Regularly review and strengthen governance controls based on lessons learned, audit outcomes, and evolving business or regulatory requirements.

title: Principal Data Engineer - Enterprise Data & Analytics - Remote
description:
The Principal Data Engineer serves as a hands-on technical authority responsible for defining and implementing enterprise-scale data architecture and engineering strategies while actively contributing to solution design, development, optimization, and technical delivery. As part of an assigned product team, this role develops and deploys data pipelines, integrations, and transformations to support analytics and machine learning applications using open-source programming languages and vendor software. The position requires a strong understanding of the organization’s current solutions, coding languages, tools, and Enterprise Data and Analytics technology framework, as well as the ability to apply independent judgment, provide consultative services to departments, divisions, and leadership committees, and partner with product owners and Analytics and Machine Learning delivery teams to identify and retrieve data, conduct exploratory analysis, transform data, visualize trends, build and validate analytical models, and translate qualitative and quantitative assessments into actionable insights.


Key responsibilities:
These positions are hands-on engineering roles. In this role, employees are expected to actively design, develop, review, and optimize production code and platform capabilities while providing technical leadership and mentorship to engineering teams.

A Bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as engineering, mathematics, computer science, information technology, health science, or other analytical/quantitative field and a minimum of seven years of professional or research experience in data visualization, data engineering, analytical modeling techniques; OR an Associate's degree in a relevant field such as engineering, mathematics, computer science, information technology, health science, or other analytical/quantitative field and a minimum of nine years of professional or research experience in data visualization, data engineering, analytical modeling techniques. In-depth business or practice knowledge will also be considered.

Incumbent must have the ability to manage a varied workload of projects with multiple priorities and stay current on healthcare trends and enterprise changes. Interpersonal skills, time management skills, and demonstrated experience working on cross functional teams are required. Requires strong analytical skills and the ability to identify and recommend solutions and a commitment to customer service. The position requires excellent verbal and written communication skills, attention to detail, and a high capacity for learning and problem resolution. Advanced experience in SQL is required. Advanced Experience in scripting languages such as Python, JavaScript, PHP, C++ or Java & API integration is required. Experience in hybrid data processing methods (batch and streaming) such as Apache Spark, Hive, Pig, Kafka is required. Experience with big data, statistics, and machine learning is required. The ability to navigate linux and windows operating systems is required. Knowledge of workflow scheduling (Apache Airflow Google Composer), Infrastructure as code (Kubernetes, Docker) CI/CD (Jenkins, Github Actions) is required. Experience in DataOps/DevOps and agile methodologies is required. Experience with hybrid data virtualization such as Denodo is preferred. Working knowledge of Tableau, Power BI, SAS, ThoughtSpot, DASH, d3, React, Snowflake, SSIS, and Google Big Query is preferred.

The preferred candidate will possess:

  • Expert-level proficiency in Python and SQL with extensive experience developing enterprise-scale production systems.
  • Advanced expertise in scalable distributed computing frameworks and modern data processing platforms.
  • Advanced experience implementing and governing open data architectures utilizing Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, Apache Hudi, and related technologies.
  • Deep understanding of modern analytical storage formats including Parquet, Avro, and ORC.
  • Demonstrated expertise in lakehouse architecture, data platform design, and large-scale data engineering practices.
  • Experience architecting and implementing cloud-agnostic solutions across multiple technology ecosystems.
  • Experience designing highly scalable, fault-tolerant, secure, and observable data platforms supporting analytics, AI, machine learning, and operational workloads.
  • Experience establishing enterprise engineering standards, architecture patterns, and modernization strategies.

title: Sommerjobb Forretningsrådgivning 2027
description:
En sommer som gir deg et innblikk i konsulentverdenen, prosjektarbeid, nytt nettverk, samt mye sosialt og moro rundt omkring i Oslo og Trondheim, sammen med en fantastisk gjeng. Høres det interessant ut?

Hver sommer ansetter vi studenter som får jobbe hos oss i en 6 ukers periode, enten i våre lokaler på toppen av Posthuset i Oslo, Powerhouse i Trondheim eller hos noen av våre kunder. Du får en unik mulighet til å bli kjent med Sopra Steria som selskap og knytte langsiktige kontakter.

Innen forretningsrådgivning kan du få muligheten til å jobbe på spennende prosjekter med for eksempel innsikt og analyse, bærekraft, prosesskartlegging- og forbedring, lønnsomhetsanalyse eller mulighetsstudier knyttet til digitalisering, for å nevne noe.

I løpet av sommeren hos oss vil du:

  • Få teste ut hvordan det er å jobbe som konsulent

  • Jobbe i team med andre sommerstudenter på reelle prosjekter

  • Bli kjent og lære sammen med erfarne Sopra Steria-konsulenter

  • Tilegne deg masse ny kunnskap gjennom prosjektarbeid og fagsamlinger

  • Få god oppfølging fra veileder

  • Delta på sosiale aktiviteter og bygge et verdifullt nettverk

Hos oss kan du på sikt jobbe som konsulent innenfor en rekke forskjellige fagområder som du kan lese mer om her. Mulighetene er mange da vi dekker hele verdikjeden i prosjekter relatert til digitalisering, innovasjon og bærekraft.

Vi ser etter deg som:

  • Er på ditt 4. studieår av en mastergrad

  • Studerer noe knyttet til forretningsrådgivning, økonomi, ledelse og organisasjonspsykologi, digital transformasjon, digitalisering i helsesektoren eller lignende

  • Tenker at det vi kan tilby, matcher dine ønsker for en sommerjobb

  • Er nysgjerrig på og motivert for å teste ut konsulentlivet

  • Har karakterer som gjør deg og de rundt deg stolte

Vi tror at du vil oppleve mestring og ha det gøy som konsulent hos oss gjennom sommeren dersom du anser deg selv som en god samarbeidspartner og relasjonsbygger. I tillegg tror vi det er en fordel å like struktur og orden, være målbevisst, profesjonell og kundeorientert.

Søknadsprosess:
Hørtes dette ut som noe for deg? Da håper vi at du vil sende oss din CV og foreløpig karakterutskrift/vitnemål. Husk å legge ved karakterutskrifter fra hele studieløpet frem til nå, inkludert VGS-karakterer. Vi ber ikke om søknadsbrev, men ønsker at du svarer på noen spørsmål som en del av søknaden. Søknader vurderes fortløpende.

Søknadsfrist: 1. oktober 2026. Søknader vurderes fortløpende.

Sommerjobbperioden i 2027 begynner i slutten av juni og varer i seks uker.

I Sopra Steria benytter vi asynkrone videointervjuer som en del av vår rekrutteringsprosess av sommerstudenter. Mer informasjon om rekrutteringsprosessen finner du ved å trykke her.

Sopra Steria har kunder og prosjekter som kan kreve sikkerhetsklarering på ulike nivåer.

Vi er Norges ledende konsulentselskap innen digitalisering, innovasjon og bærekraft. I Sopra Steria bistår vi våre kunder innen privat og offentlig sektor med å bli fremtidens virksomheter. I en årrekke har vi vært rangert som en av Norges beste arbeidsplasser. Du finner oss i Oslo, Stavanger, Trondheim, Bergen, Drammen, Hamar, Fredrikstad, Kristiansand og Tromsø.

  • Prior experience in designing with x86 and/or ARM processors.

  • Prior experience in designing with DDR4/DDR5 memory, PCIe, SATA, USB.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

title: Customer Team Member

Customer Team Member

As a Customer Team Member, you’ll work as part of a friendly team in a fast-moving Co-op store, helping deliver essential services to your community every day. Depending on your store, this could involve working in our post office, or bakery, or helping with online services by picking and packing orders for home delivery. You’ll help keep our shelves stocked and support sales, making sure customers can find what they need. You’ll be a familiar face in the community, getting to know your customers and helping us stay connected with local and national charities. Plus, you’ll promote Co-op membership, helping more customers enjoy the benefits of our unique business.

  • Make sure the store safe and legal – keep the shelves stocked and make sure prices, dates, and temperatures are all as they should be

  • The ability to work flexibly across a number of shifts and as part of a team

Why Co-op?
At Co-op, we're owned by our members. And because we're owned by you, we can do right by you. So, when you join us, you're not just taking a job, you're joining a movement. We're an organisation that puts people and communities first, and we're powered by purpose. We want this to be a place where you can thrive, so you'll also receive:
  • Full training and career development resources
  • 30% discount on all Co-op products in-store
  • Flexible access to your pay as you earn it
  • A pension scheme with up to 10% employer contributions
  • 31 days of holiday (including bank holidays, pro rata for part time colleagues)
  • 24/7 access to GP appointments, and colleague support programme
  • Cycle-to-work scheme
  • Market-leading policies to help you through life's big moments

  • Commercial and industrial sites across the Edmonton and Calgary areas, plus out of town camp projects
  • Outdoor work at heights, year round, in all Alberta weather conditions
  • Camp accommodation provided when working out of town
  • Safe, team oriented culture with PPE and site safety standards enforced
What We Offer
  • $36.00 per hour for 3rd Year apprentices, $30.00 per hour for 2nd Year apprentices

  • Full-time, permanent work with a busy company and room to advance
  • Hands on hours and journeyman mentorship toward your Red Seal ticket
  • Blue Cross benefits after 3 months, including dental, extended health, and vision
  • Camp accommodation on out of town projects
  • A safe, team oriented crew that looks out for each other

title: Technical Project Manager (DORA Implementation)
description:
As a Technical Project Manager, you will lead the hands-on implementation of the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) across multiple client entities. Acting as the bridge between regulatory requirements and operational execution, you will coordinate stakeholders, drive implementation activities, monitor progress, and support both technical and business teams in achieving DORA compliance.

Key Responsibilities

Project Planning & Delivery

  • Maintain and drive the DORA implementation roadmap, ensuring clear milestones, deliverables, and timelines.
  • Translate regulatory requirements into actionable implementation plans and cybersecurity framework requirements.
  • Monitor progress across entities and proactively identify risks, dependencies, and delays.
  • Support entities in addressing technical and operational challenges throughout the implementation journey.

Stakeholder Management & Coordination

  • Coordinate and facilitate steering committees, workshops, follow-up meetings, and ad hoc checkpoints.
  • Organize regular health checks ("quick-check" sessions) to assess implementation progress and address roadblocks.
  • Ensure alignment among business, IT, cybersecurity, and management stakeholders.

Communication & Reporting

  • Prepare and deliver clear status reports, dashboards, executive summaries, and one-page briefs for various stakeholder groups.
  • Communicate project progress, upcoming actions, risks, and responsibilities in a concise and impactful manner.
  • Maintain project documentation, including FAQs, SharePoint repositories, lessons learned, and implementation guidance.

Technical Implementation Support

  • Work closely with technical and business teams to support the implementation of DORA requirements.
  • Contribute to topics such as:
    • Network segmentation
    • Backup and recovery processes
    • Third-party risk monitoring
    • Operational resilience controls
    • Cybersecurity governance practices
  • Assist in troubleshooting implementation challenges and coordinate remediation actions.

Point of Contact

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned stakeholders regarding DORA-related topics.

description:

title: Senior Director, Product Finance

About Sandy Hook Promise
Sandy Hook Promise (SHP) envisions a future where all children are free from school shootings and other acts of violence. As a national nonprofit organization, SHP’s mission is to educate and empower youth and adults to prevent violence in schools, homes, and communities. Creators of the lifesaving, evidence-informed Know the Signs prevention programs, SHP teaches the warning signs of someone who may be in crisis, socially isolated, or at-risk of hurting themselves or others and how to get help. SHP also advances school safety, youth mental health, and responsible gun ownership at the state and federal levels through nonpartisan policy and partnerships.

SHP is led by several family members whose loved ones were killed in the tragic mass shooting at Sandy Hook Elementary School on December 14, 2012.

Commitment to Belonging, Community, Engagement, and Respect
SHP strives to ensure its culture and work environment reflect the values of belonging, community, engagement and respect. We actively seek to understand and respond to the diverse perspectives and lived experiences of individuals across socioeconomic backgrounds, rural and urban communities, and diversity of thought, in addition to traditional protected categories. We are committed to ensuring that every SHP employee feels heard, valued, and a true sense of belonging. SHP encourages individuals who share our commitment to these core values and to our mission to apply.

Location
We are a U.S. based organization and most of our staff work remotely. This role will require 15% travel (on an as-needed basis).

Candidates should reside within a reasonable distance (30-miles) of a major airport to ensure efficient, cost-effective travel. Team members are expected to make thoughtful travel decisions that balance cost, convenience, and sustainability.

About the Role
The Director or Senior Director of Learning Architecture, Professional Learning serves as the organizational lead for designing and operationalizing high-impact, evidence-based learning strategies for educators, educational staff, administrators, and out-of-school time (OST) professionals at Sandy Hook Promise (SHP). This senior role is responsible for defining and executing a long-term vision for scalable, accessible, and effective professional learning across asynchronous, virtual, and in-person modalities that supports program fidelity, implementation quality, capacity development, and school and community impact.

Drawing on deep expertise in curriculum and professional learning design, development, and facilitation, this leader translates research into practical, user-centered learning solutions that support effective implementation of SHP's violence prevention programs. They provide leadership in train-the-trainer models, educational strategy, and cross-functional alignment to advance SHP's strategic priorities, innovation, and program effectiveness.

Job Responsibilities Include (but are not limited to)

Strategic Vision & Ownership

  • Develop and lead the strategic vision for SHP's professional learning architecture, ensuring alignment with organizational goals, partner needs, best practices, and field trends.
  • Translate strategy into actionable plans, roadmaps, metrics, and accountability measures to drive implementation and results.

Professional Learning Materials

  • Oversee the design, development, writing, and continuous improvement of educator-facing materials, implementation resources, and tools that support high-quality program delivery and fidelity.
  • Manage external subject matter experts, consultants, contractors, and vendors to ensure projects are delivered on time, within scope, and aligned with organizational standards.
  • Ensure materials incorporate evidence-based approaches, implementation science, violence prevention, and related frameworks, while remaining practical and adaptable across school, district, OST, and regional settings.
  • Align all professional learning materials with the needs of Program Implementation teams.

Train-the-Trainer & Professional Development Strategy

  • Lead the design, development, and writing of scalable train-the-trainer systems and professional learning offerings.
  • Direct the development of program-agnostic learning opportunities through SHP Learning Studio to meet evolving educator and staff needs.
  • Ensure learning experiences are aligned with adult learning principles, program theories of change, and implementation goals.
  • Partner across teams to integrate professional learning into training and technical assistance models.

Annual Planning, Monitoring & Reporting

  • Lead annual planning for the Professional Learning team, aligning priorities, resources, and improvement efforts with organizational goals.
  • Monitor progress through established metrics and provide regular updates to executive leadership on outcomes, risks, trends, and recommended adjustments.
  • Use internal and external data to identify opportunities for improvement and inform strategic decision-making.

Data-Informed Continuous Improvement

  • Partner with Evaluation and Quality Improvement teams to pilot, assess, and refine professional learning offerings using feedback and impact data.
  • Establish and monitor KPIs related to engagement, learning outcomes, implementation quality, and program effectiveness.
  • Apply continuous improvement and implementation science principles to strengthen learning strategies and outcomes.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Represent Professional Learning on cross-functional committees, initiatives, and leadership forums.
  • Proactively identify, communicate, and address risks, opportunities, and operational challenges affecting goals, implementation, or sustainability.
  • Keep leadership informed of progress, challenges, and recommended actions to support timely decision-making and strategic adjustments.
  • Collaborate across departments to advance organizational priorities and support successful program implementation.
  • Perform other duties as assigned based on organizational needs.
  • A commitment to SHP’s mission and values. (do not remove)
Desired Skills and Experience
  • Master's degree or higher in Adult Education, K-12 Education, Curriculum & Instruction, or a related field required.
  • 7+ years of experience designing, developing, and writing professional learning for educators, youth-serving professionals, or related audiences.
  • 10+ years of experience working with K-12 school systems, out-of-school time (OST) programs, community-based education settings, or similar learning environments.
  • Desired Skills and Experience
  • Master's degree or higher in Adult Education, K-12 Education, Curriculum & Instruction, or a related field required.
  • 7+ years of experience designing, developing, and writing professional learning for educators, youth-serving professionals, or related audiences.
  • 10+ years of experience working with K-12 school systems, out-of-school time (OST) programs, community-based education settings, or similar learning environments.
Benefits and Salary Range
The salary range for this position is $110,000-$120,000.
SHP uses a structured internal rubric to guide salary placement and ensure equitable pay. Typically, new hires are placed at the start of the salary range to ensure equity with current employees, and as a practice, we do not negotiate salaries.
  • SHP offers a competitive benefits package, including:
    • Unlimited PTO
    • Flexible schedules
    • Paid holidays and 10 days sick leave
    • Paid parental leave
    • Health, dental, and vision
    • Employer paid life insurance and short- and long-term disability
    • 401k match
    • Professional development stipend
    • Wellness & mental health support
    • Employer Paid Employee Assistance Program.
Our organization operates within a distributed workforce, allowing for location flexibility across the country for most positions. We provide remote office support for all staff, which includes a laptop, home office reimbursement, monthly Wi-Fi reimbursement up to $40, and monthly cell phone reimbursement up to $50.

Additional Instructions
  • Interested SHP staff and volunteers are invited to apply by Friday, August 7, 2026, and should notify HR and Talent Acquisition upon submission.
  • Applications will close on Friday, September 4, 2026. All are welcome to apply.
  • Please note: applicants must be based in the U.S. Thank you!
Equal Opportunity Employment
SHP is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We strive to be an employer of choice: where a diverse mix of talented people want to come and do their best work. SHP does not make employment related decisions based on race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. We are focused on promoting multiculturalism and inclusion so that all SHP employees feel valued and respected. We believe deeply that a diverse workforce comprised of people of all beliefs, backgrounds, and life experiences who seek to prevent gun violence and stop the tragic loss of life will make SHP a stronger, more effective organization.

title: Engagement Lead - Data Science
description:
At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections, where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.

The Position

Engagement Lead - Data Science

Roche India - Roche Services & Solutions

Hyderabad or Chennai

A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love.

That’s what makes us Roche.

Roche has established the Global Analytics and Technology Center of Excellence (GATE) as part of Roche Services & Solutions (RSS) India to drive analytics and technology-driven solutions by partnering with Roche affiliates across the globe. RSS is a global division operating in an agile organizational setup without extensive hierarchical structure, where all our employees lead from every seat, and inspirational leadership, and an entrepreneurial customer-centric mindset are our core values.

Your Opportunity

As an Engagement Lead - Data Science, you will provide technical leadership across two sub-teams: the Predictive AI team and the Causal & Experimentation AI team. In this role, you will architect advanced enterprise AI solutions, mentor data science talent, and serve as a strategic consultant across global business lines including Commercial, R&D, Diagnostics etc.

Beyond team delivery, you will play a pivotal leadership role within the broader GATE organization—actively driving GATE-level people initiatives, talent capability enablement, strategic product development roadmaps, and cross-center innovation activities.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Technical Leadership & Mentorship: Lead, mentor, and guide Senior Data Scientists and Data Scientists across Predictive AI and Causal & Experimentation AI sub-teams, fostering technical excellence, modular coding standards, and agile delivery practices.

  • Strategic Business Consulting: Act as a trusted AI consultant to global business partners across to translate complex business challenges into actionable Data Science and AI strategies.

  • GATE-Level Leadership & Product Development: Champion GATE-wide initiatives by actively shaping center-level AI product development strategy, contributing to talent enablement and mentorship programs, and driving standard methodologies across the GATE ecosystem.

  • Rapid Prototyping & Business Value: Rapidly design and build Proofs of Concept (POCs), prototypes, and business case studies to demonstrate tangible ROI and secure executive buy-in.

  • Predictive & Causal AI Solutions: Architect and oversee the development of robust predictive models, causal inference frameworks, and experimental designs (A/B testing, quasi-experiments) to drive decision-making.

  • GenAI & Agentic Frameworks: Drive the strategy and implementation of enterprise Generative AI architectures, including Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), fine-tuning techniques, and Agentic AI workflows.

  • End-to-End MLOps & Infrastructure: Partner with MLOps and Data Engineering teams to design, operationalize, and maintain end-to-end ML/AI pipelines, ensuring scalable model deployment, continuous monitoring, and automated lifecycle management.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with global cross-functional stakeholders in an agile environment, conducting demos, reviews, and retrospectives to continuously improve team deliverables.

Who You Are

  • You hold a bachelors or Master’s in Data science, Statistics, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, Computer Science, Business Analytics, Technology or other related quantitative fields and 12+ years of overall experience in Data Science/AI, with at least 5+ years in leading analytic/ AI product lifecycle and mentorship role guiding AI teams. Experience in Pharmaceutical or Healthcare domain (US/Europe market context) an advantgae

  • Renowned and globally recognized professional certifications in Data Science, Machine Learning, Generative AI, Prompt Engineering, Cloud AI Platforms, or advanced Analytics are advantageous

  • You are an accomplished AI practitioner and technical lead who thrives in fast-paced, agile engineering environments. You remain close to the code, balancing deep hands-on expertise with a focus on designing, automating, and deploying robust, end-to-end AI systems. Operating at the intersection of Predictive, Causal, and Generative AI, you architect scalable AI automation solutions, mentor engineering talent, and translate complex technical outcomes into strategic business impact for executive stakeholders

  • Predictive & Causal AI: Deep expertise in advanced machine learning, predictive modeling, causal inference methods, and experimental design (A/B testing, econometrics)

  • Generative & Agentic AI: Hands-on experience with LLMs, Prompt Engineering, RAG, and Fine-tuning techniques. Proven capability building multi-agent architectures using Agentic AI frameworks such as LangChain, AutoGen, or CrewAI

  • MLOps Lifecycle & Cloud: Demonstrated experience designing and maintaining end-to-end MLOps pipelines using platforms such as MLflow, Kubeflow, or AWS SageMaker. Proficiency with containerization and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes) and AWS cloud infrastructure

  • Core Programming & Data Pipelines: Expert proficiency in Python and SQL. Strong experience with modern backend pipeline development tools such as PySpark, and Git/CI/CD pipelines

  • Demonstrated ability to consult with executive stakeholders, present business cases, and manage global cross-functional relationships.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with an agile mindset and strong attention to quality.

Note: This job description is intended as a general guideline for the responsibilities and qualifications required for this position. It is not an exhaustive list, and responsibilities may evolve and change based on business needs.

Who we are

A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. title: Table Games Supervisor
description:
The Table Games Supervisor oversees the operation of assigned table games to ensure accurate gameplay, regulatory compliance, and exceptional guest experience. This role is responsible for maintaining strict control of cards, chips, and equipment; monitoring play for irregularities, advantage play, or potential cheating; and ensuring that all game procedures are followed consistently and correctly. The Supervisor supports and guides dealers in delivering efficient, accurate, and professional game operations - including timely and correct payment of winning bets - while ensuring the safety and security of guests, team members, and table assets.

Additionally, the position requires delivering outstanding guest service, resolving disputes, and assisting with the management of table funds, fills, credits, player ratings, and documentation. The Supervisor is expected to maintain strong knowledge of property amenities, promotions, and events, and to consistently present a friendly, welcoming, and professional demeanor. Other duties may be assigned as needed to support casino and departmental operations.

  • Monitor table game activity continuously to ensure accuracy, adherence to procedures, and protection of game integrity.

  • Manage and safeguard all gaming cards, equipment, and assets.

  • Ensure proper use of the table, shoe, paddle, and all required equipment.

  • Oversee and verify accurate, timely payouts and correct dealer errors when necessary.

  • Oversee administrative functions including table fills, credits, player ratings, and game rundowns.

  • Assist with monitoring staffing levels to ensure proper coverage and adherence to labor budgets.

  • Identify and analyze guest play patterns to detect potential cheating, scams, card counting, or unusual play activity.

  • Maintain strict confidentiality regarding financial information, company policies, procedures, and both guest and team member information.

  • Ensure compliance with all regulatory requirements and company policies.

  • Support ongoing improvement of dealer skill levels and customer service standards.

  • Maintain a clean, organized, and professional work environment.

  • Ensure the safety and security of all guests and team members on and around assigned tables.

  • Remain knowledgeable of all casino events, promotions, and special activities.

  • Perform all duties in a high‑volume, fast‑paced environment while managing frequent time pressures.

  • Complete additional tasks or reasonable requests from management as assigned.

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

  • High school diploma or GED preferred.
  • Technical school training or previous casino experience dealing table games preferred.
  • Proficiency in all casino table games offered is required.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a valid Colorado Gaming License.
  • Must be able to work any assigned shift, including late nights, weekends, holidays, and overtime as needed.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Ability to read, write, and understand basic instructions in English.
  • Strong verbal communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Excellent eye‑hand coordination and ability to make accurate, rapid calculations of chips and currency for payout purposes.
  • Knowledge of cheating methods, theft techniques, and advantage‑play behaviors.
  • Ability to perform duties accurately in a high‑volume, fast‑paced environment with frequent interruptions and time constraints.
