title: Senior Marine Structures Engineer
description:
Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.

We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.

Role description:

We are seeking a Senior Marine Structures Engineer to act as the marine and coastal technical authority on site for our construction supervision team in Vancouver. The role is suited to a specialist who has built a career around waterfront and in water structures and who is comfortable carrying professional responsibility for that work while it is being built.

This is a full-time field-based position. The Senior Marine Structures Engineer supports the site team during Engineering Services During Construction as marine works move from design completion through installation, testing and completion certification, covering quay walls, wharves, jetties, dolphins, marine piling, sheet pile and combi wall systems, revetments, breakwaters, scour protection, cofferdams, marine access structures and associated temporary works.

The position carries Engineer of Record responsibility for the marine structures under supervision, including the conduct and documentation of field reviews, the assessment of departures from the design basis, and the certification that the constructed marine works substantially conform with the design. The role is not a design office position and does not involve production work in structural analysis or modelling software. What is required is the judgement to read a marine structure as it is being built and to reach a sound position on it.

Role accountabilities:

In this role you will act as the Engineer of Record for the marine structures under your supervision. You will set and carry out the field review programme for marine works, document each review, apply your professional seal where required, and certify that the constructed works substantially conform with the design documents and the applicable codes. Where an as-built condition departs from the design basis, you will assess the effect on capacity, durability and service life and set out a clear engineering position on acceptance, repair or replacement.

You will review contractor submissions for the marine works, including piling method statements, driveability assessments, pile driving records, welding and coating procedures, marine concrete placement methods, precast handling and lifting plans, temporary works designs and marine spread arrangements, and you will confirm that each is consistent with the design assumptions.

You will attend and witness marine construction activities, covering pile installation and set criteria, tolerance verification, underwater placement, backfilling behind retaining structures, armour and filter layer placement, and geotextile and scour protection installation. You will confirm hold points, release work for cover, and record what you have seen in a form that stands up later.

You will interpret geotechnical, survey and bathymetric information as it becomes available, comparing it against the design basis, and you will advise on the treatment of variable seabed conditions, obstructions, over dredge and unexpected material. You will review dredging and backfill records against the design profiles and support the resolution of the change that follows.

You will provide technical direction on marine durability, including cathodic protection, coating systems, concrete cover and mix design in the tidal and splash zones, and on the corrosion, allowances applied to steel elements. You will support the assessment of berthing and mooring arrangements, fender and bollard installation and load testing.

You will support underwater inspection planning, direct the dive team on what is to be inspected and recorded, and review dive and survey reporting against the acceptance criteria. You will contribute to the non conformance process on the marine works, support the engineering assessment of any claim turning on marine conditions, weather downtime or seabed variability, and mentor engineers developing their marine experience on site.

Qualifications & Experience:

  • Minimum 15 years of engineering experience with a clear specialization in marine, coastal and waterfront structures on ports, terminals, harbours or heavy civil marine projects, including substantial site-based construction supervision
  • Bachelor’s degree in civil or Structural Engineering. A postgraduate qualification in coastal, maritime or structural engineering is an asset
  • Registration as a Professional Engineer with EGBC, or eligibility for registration, is an asset. Registration is expected before mobilization for candidates who will carry Engineer of Record duties and seal field review and assurance documentation. Equivalent international registration such as CEng MICE or CPEng is well regarded
  • Demonstrated experience acting as, or supporting, the Engineer of Record for marine structures during construction, including documented field reviews and certification of substantial conformance
  • Demonstrated construction supervision experience across quay walls, wharves, jetties, marine piling, breakwaters, revetments and scour protection
  • Working knowledge of the codes and guidance applied to marine works in Canada and internationally, including CSA S6, CSA S16, CSA A23.1, BS 6349 and PIANC guidance
  • Practical understanding of marine construction methods and marine plant, including barges, jack up platforms, floating and crawler cranes, impact and vibratory hammers, dredgers and survey vessels
  • Understanding of tidal, wave, current, and ice loading considerations and their impact on construction sequencing along the British Columbia coast
  • Awareness of federal and provincial environmental requirements affecting in water work, including fisheries timing windows and turbidity control
  • Ability to direct and interpret underwater inspection, marine survey and instrumentation output during construction
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain a marine technical position to non-specialist stakeholders
  • Willingness to be based full time on site and to work from marine plant and vessels, including work outside standard hours and within tidal windows
  • Valid driving license and the site and marine safety certification required for site and vessel access

Why Arcadis?

We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It’s why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.

You’ll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you’ll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.

Together, we can create a lasting legacy.

Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging

We want you to be able to bring your best self to work every day which is why we take equality and inclusion seriously and hold ourselves to account for our actions. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice and provide a great place to work for all our people. We are an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. Women, minorities, people with disabilities and veterans are strongly encouraged to apply. We are dedicated to a policy of non-discrimination in employment on any basis including race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, disability, veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

title: Head of Partner Ecosystem & Growth-Payments-Executive Director
description:
You are a strategic and analytical executive leader who is passionate about delivering solutions to clients through impactful partnerships.


As the Head of Partner Ecosystem and Growth you will drive the adoption of JPMC Merchant Services solutions and the expansion of its commerce ecosystem. You will define and execute the partnership ecosystem strategy by building deep partner relationships, shaping commercial and technical engagements, and aligning with the right partners to deliver best-in-class client experiences. You will also grow and support a vibrant developer and partner community to enable seamless integration of commerce solutions across verticals and regions, driving the long-term success and scale of JPMC Commerce Solutions. The candidate should have experience influencing product, sales, and technology transformations in the payments industry, with a strong understanding of how companies leverage payment providers globally (direct Merchant Services experience is a plus). Comfort working cross-functionally with Operations, Sales, Finance, and Product is essential to expand the acquiring organization internationally and grow an existing ~$1Bn revenue base, while streamlining communication, prioritizing competing efforts, and driving outcomes for the broader organization.

Merchant Services is the global payment processing business for JPMorgan Chase & Co. Merchant Services is the world’s leading merchant acquirer with over $2.2 trillion in annual transaction volume. Merchant Services is a leading provider of payment, fraud and data security for companies large and small and capable of authorizing transactions in more than 130 currencies. The organization is engaging in a multi-year international expansion, platform modernization, all while serving some of the largest company names on the planet.

Job responsibilities

  • Ecosystem Strategy & Vision: Build and nurture a thriving ecosystem of partner integrations for in-store, eCommerce and omnichannel merchant services that creates value for clients and partners, drives growth and innovation, and increases revenue for JPMC Merchant Services.
  • Partnership Development: Identify and forge strategic partnerships with key stakeholders including developers, industry leaders, and ecosystem collaborators
  • Ecosystem Support & Enablement: Create and launch scalable partner programs, including enablement, co-marketing, and co-selling initiatives by bridging internal teams (Sales, Marketing, Commercialization, Product, Tech, Corporate Development & Partnerships) with external partners for aligned goals and execution.
  • Product Integration & Adoption: Work closely with large group of our internal stakeholders (engineering, marketing, solutions, product) to ensure Commerce Solutions are easily accessible and integrated into a wide range of applications.
  • Ecosystem Metrics & Reporting: Define key performance indicators (KPIs) for ecosystem growth, tracking the progress of the organization’s efforts in growing the partner and developer base.
  • Ecosystem Events & Activation: Lead key events such as developer meetups, and conferences that promote the growth of the JPMC Commerce ecosystem and provide valuable networking opportunities for developers and industry leaders.
  • Evaluate new business models quickly and with financial discipline, driving decisive outcomes that are agreed to by all stakeholders and then turned over for execution or removed from ideation
  • Identify sales distribution channels for regional priorities and influence the global sales force for optimal P&L gains through direct client sales, partner distributions, or other commercial efforts to grow the global P&L
  • Drive increased revenue through partners, by executing joint go-to market motions with other commercialization, marketing and sales teams to close deals.

Required qualifications, skills and capabilities

  • 10+ years’ experience of experience in partner ecosystem development and commercialization across payment, commerce and/or technology industries.
  • Proven track record of building and scaling developer ecosystems, partnerships, and community engagement in a fast-paced, rapidly evolving space.
  • Strong business acumen with experience in strategic partnerships, negotiation, and driving the growth of developer communities and ecosystems as well as expertise in go to market, product marketing, and sales strategies
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders, including developers, partners.
  • Ability to translate complex technical concepts into accessible language for developers, partners, and external audiences.
  • Demonstrated leadership and people management skills, with the ability to inspire and collaborate with cross-functional teams, including engineering, marketing, and product.
  • Data-driven approach with experience in tracking, measuring, and reporting on ecosystem growth metrics and KPIs.
  • Excellent time management, communication, organization and project management skills
  • Energetic, self-motivated and effective under pressure - must enjoy the challenge of working autonomously within a fast-paced and demanding working environment
  • Demonstrates communication and diplomacy skills to work cross-organizationally to influence others, propel results/change and implement projects/processes on simultaneous projects

FEDERAL DEPOSIT INSURANCE ACT:

This position is subject to Section 19 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act. As such, an employment offer for this position is contingent on JPMorganChase’s review of criminal conviction history, including pretrial diversions or program entries.

title: Product Portfolio Director – Digital Energy Products
description:
We are looking for a Digital Product Portfolio Director to shape the future of DNV's portfolio of digital products and data-driven solutions supporting critical energy infrastructure.

This is a highly strategic leadership role for an experienced digital product professional who can operate across products, platforms, markets, and business lines. You will play a key role in helping DNV navigate the rapidly evolving energy landscape by ensuring our digital product portfolio continues to create value for customers, supports business growth, and strengthens our market position.

The digital portfolio has evolved over time through a number of independent products, each addressing specific customer needs and market opportunities. As the portfolio matures, there is a significant opportunity to create greater value by strengthening strategic alignment, leveraging shared capabilities, and adopting a more platform-centric approach. You will play a pivotal role in shaping this evolution, working with Product Managers to help transform a collection of successful products into a more cohesive, scalable, and market-leading product ecosystem.

What you will do

  • Define and own the long-term digital product portfolio and platform strategy, aligning investments, product direction, and platform evolution with business objectives, customer needs, and market opportunities.
  • Lead the transformation of independent product lines into a cohesive, platform-driven product ecosystem with a clear strategic identity, differentiated value proposition, and scalable operating model.
  • Challenge, coach, and mentor product teams, implementing professional product management practices and ensuring portfolio-wide alignment around customer value, business outcomes, and long-term growth objectives.
  • Drive portfolio investment, prioritization, and lifecycle decisions, balancing innovation, growth opportunities, platform development, modernization, and product rationalization.
  • Establish strategic governance across the portfolio, ensuring product roadmaps contribute meaningfully to the long-term portfolio vision while enabling alignment between product, technology, and business priorities.
  • Continuously assess portfolio performance to identify gaps, overlaps, risks, and emerging opportunities, recommending optimization actions that maximize customer impact, commercial value, and competitive advantage.
  • Serve as the principal strategic advisor to Product, Technology, and Business teams, challenging and influencing portfolio investment decisions, strategic priorities, and long-term direction through insight, credibility, and market expertise.

Success in this role requires a unique combination of digital product leadership, strategic thinking, commercial awareness, coaching and mentoring, and influence. You will partner with Product Managers, Technology leaders, Commercial teams, and senior stakeholders across the organization to guide decisions, challenge assumptions, and ensure the portfolio evolves in line with customer needs, market dynamics, and long-term business objectives.

  • 10+ years of experience in Digital Product Management, including at least 5 years in Product Portfolio Management, with a proven track record of defining, scaling, and optimizing digital products and product portfolios within complex global organizations.

title: Senior Wet Utilities Engineer
description:
Arcadis is the world's leading company delivering sustainable design, engineering, and consultancy solutions for natural and built assets.

We are more than 34,000 people, in over 30 countries, dedicated to improving quality of life. Everyone has an important role to play. With the power of many curious minds, together we can solve the world’s most complex challenges and deliver more impact together.

Role description:

We are seeking a Senior Wet Utilities Engineer to support the field delivery of site infrastructure works in Vancouver. The role suits an engineer with a strong background in buried services and water infrastructure on heavy civil, ports, marine and major infrastructure projects, and with the site experience to see that work built and tested correctly.

This is a full-time site-based position. The Senior Wet Utilities Engineer provides the wet utilities technical lead during Engineering Services During Construction, covering potable water, firewater, sanitary sewer, storm drainage, treated and process water, pumping stations, chambers, outfalls, culverts, dewatering systems, hydraulic controls, stormwater management facilities, oil water separators and associated utility corridors and crossings.

The position carries Engineer of Record responsibility for the wet utility installations under supervision, including the conduct and documentation of field reviews, the witnessing of pressure, leakage and performance testing, and the certification that the installed systems substantially conform with the design and the requirements of the utility owners and authorities having jurisdiction. The role is not a design office position and does not involve production work in hydraulic modelling or drafting software.

Role accountabilities:

In this role you will act as the Engineer of Record for the wet utility works under your supervision. You will set and carry out the field review programme, document each review, apply your professional seal where required, and certify substantial conformance with the design documents, the specifications and the requirements of the municipal and utility authorities involved.

You will review contractor submissions for wet utility works, including installation method statements, trench support and dewatering proposals, bedding and backfill details, pipe material and fitting submittals, thrust restraint details, chamber and pump station details and testing procedures.

You will supervise the re routing, demolition and installation of buried and above ground utility systems on site, covering trenching and shoring, pipe laying, jointing and welding, thrust blocks and restraint, chamber and manhole construction, valve and hydrant installation, service connections and the reinstatement of surfaces and surrounds, stormwater outfalls, and you will hold the line on inspection before backfilling.

You will witness and review testing and acceptance activity, including pressure and leakage testing, disinfection and bacteriological clearance for potable systems, inspection and mandrel testing for gravity systems, infiltration and exfiltration testing, and pump station functional and performance testing, and you will confirm that the records support acceptance and handover.

You will coordinate utility diversions, protections and connections with the relevant municipal and utility authorities, supporting permit and approval submissions, tie in planning, shutdown coordination and the phasing needed to keep existing services in operation during construction.

You will manage the interface between wet utilities and the earthworks, roads, structures, electrical and control packages, including duct and pipe crossings, cover and clearance requirements, and the instrumentation and control associated with pumping and treatment plant. You will support the non conformance process, review record and operation and maintenance documentation, and mentor engineers and inspectors working on utility packages.

Qualifications & Experience:

  • Minimum 12-15 years of civil or water engineering experience on heavy civil, ports, marine, municipal or large infrastructure projects, the greater part of it site based, with substantial field delivery of wet utility systems
  • Bachelor’s degree in civil, Environmental or Water Resources Engineering
  • Registration as a Professional Engineer with EGBC, or eligibility for registration, is an asset. Registration is expected before mobilisation for candidates who will carry Engineer of Record duties and seal field review and assurance documentation. Equivalent Canadian or international registration is welcomed
  • Demonstrated experience acting as, or supporting, the Engineer of Record during construction, including documented field reviews, witnessing of testing and certification of substantial conformance for utility packages
  • Working knowledge of MMCD, the BC Ministry of Transportation and Infrastructure specifications, AWWA standards, the BC Plumbing Code, NFPA requirements for firewater and applicable stormwater management guidance
  • Demonstrated site experience with pressure and gravity systems in ductile iron, HDPE, PVC, steel and concrete, including jointing methods, restraint and corrosion protection in coastal and saline ground
  • Practical construction and commissioning experience with pumping stations, wet wells, outfalls, oil water separators and stormwater treatment installations
  • Familiarity with trenchless methods such as horizontal directional drilling, auger boring and pipe jacking is an asset
  • Understanding of provincial and federal environmental requirements affecting drainage, discharge and works near water
  • Ability to read utility drawings, survey information and test records in the field and to reconcile them against the installed condition
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills and experience coordinating with municipalities, utility owners and regulators on an active site
  • Willingness to be based full time on site, including tie in and shutdown work outside standard hours
  • Valid driving licence and the site safety certification required for construction site access, including confined space entry awareness

Why Arcadis?

We can only achieve our goals when everyone is empowered to be their best. We believe everyone's contribution matters. It’s why we are pioneering a skills-based approach, where you can harness your unique experience and expertise to carve your career path and maximize the impact we can make together.

You’ll do meaningful work, and no matter what role, you’ll be helping to deliver sustainable solutions for a more prosperous planet. Make your mark, on your career, your colleagues, your clients, your life and the world around you.

Together, we can create a lasting legacy.

Join Arcadis. Create a Legacy.

Our Commitment to Equality, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging

We want you to be able to bring your best self to work every day which is why we take equality and inclusion seriously and hold ourselves to account for our actions. Our ambition is to be an employer of choice and provide a great place to work for all our people. We are an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. Women, minorities, people with disabilities and veterans are strongly encouraged to apply. We are dedicated to a policy of non-discrimination in employment on any basis including race, creed, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, citizenship status, disability, veteran status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

title: Senior Project Manager — Nuclear Power Generation
description:
AECOM is seeking a Senior Project Manager to lead delivery of complex projects in the nuclear power generation industry. This role is accountable for project success—including scope, safety, quality, financial performance, schedule, and client satisfaction—while also contributing to business development through a seller–doer model. The Senior Project Manager leads multi-disciplinary teams, manages nuclear quality and regulatory expectations, and partners with clients to identify and convert new work opportunities.

For this role, AECOM offers the freedom and flexibility to work remotely and/or be located at a variety of Energy offices located in multiple locations across the United States.

The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:

  • Lead end-to-end delivery of nuclear power generation projects (e.g., plant modifications, life extension, uprates, new equipment integration, engineering studies, licensing support, outage support, and capital programs).
  • Establish delivery approach, governance, and execution plans, aligning scope, deliverables, milestones, and acceptance criteria with client expectations.
  • Direct multi-disciplinary teams (engineering, environmental, licensing, project controls, procurement support, construction/outage coordination as applicable) and manage subcontractors/vendors.
  • Drive strong interface management across plant stakeholders (operations, maintenance, engineering, licensing, supply chain, and site leadership).
  • Ensure effective closeout, lessons learned, and transition to operations where applicable.
  • Maintain a strong nuclear safety culture and ensure work is planned and executed with appropriate rigor, conservative decision-making, and accountability.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory and quality requirements (e.g., client QA programs. ISO 9001, 10 CFR 50 Appendix B, NQA-1, configuration management, document control, records retention) as required by contract and project scope.
  • Oversee technical reviews and verification/validation activities; ensure deliverables are complete, traceable, and audit-ready.
  • Manage project risk, including nuclear safety, regulatory, schedule, and supply chain risks; implement mitigation plans and corrective actions as appropriate and relevant to AECOM’s scope.
  • Own project financial performance: budgeting, forecasting, cost control, revenue recognition inputs, invoicing coordination, and margin outcomes.
  • Lead schedule development and performance management, including resource loading and critical path awareness; drive recovery plans when needed.
  • Control scope and change management: evaluate impacts, negotiate equitable adjustments, document approvals, and maintain contract compliance.
  • Provide clear internal and client reporting (KPIs, earned value/progress, risk register status, and executive summaries).
  • Serve as primary client interface and trusted advisor; maintain strong working relationships at multiple levels (PM, engineering managers, licensing, and site leadership).
  • Proactively manage expectations, communicate progress and risks, and resolve issues early to protect nuclear safety, delivery outcomes, and client confidence.
  • Facilitate decision-making through clear recommendations, option analysis, and documented action plans.
  • Identify, qualify, and pursue follow-on work with existing nuclear clients and strategic accounts; support account planning and pipeline development.
  • Contribute to the US nuclear strategy development
  • Lead or support capture activities: client discovery, solution shaping, teaming, pricing strategy inputs, and risk/opportunity evaluation.
  • Contribute to proposals and interviews: scope definition, execution approach, staffing plans, schedule basis, and technical narrative development.
  • Maintain awareness of nuclear market trends (fleet life extension, digital modernization, reliability, carbon-free generation strategy, SMR/advanced reactor ecosystem where applicable) to support growth conversations.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline (or equivalent relevant experience).
  • 8 years of experience delivering projects in the nuclear power generation industry (utility, OEM, EPC/AE, or nuclear consultancy).
  • Demonstrated success managing complex, high-stakes projects with accountability for scope, schedule, and budget.
  • Experience and understanding of nuclear industry expectations related to safety culture, QA, configuration management, and document rigor.
  • Proven client-facing leadership and experience supporting pursuits/proposals or expanding client scope.
  • Ability to meet site access requirements (background checks, fitness-for-duty, security badging) when required by the client as a condition of ongoing employment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • PMP (or equivalent) and/or advanced technical degree.
  • Familiarity with NQA-1 programs and/or regulated nuclear design environments; experience working under client 10 CFR 50 Appendix B programs (as applicable).
  • Experience leading multi-office teams and managing subcontractors/suppliers in a regulated environment.
  • Experience coordinating with field teams and supporting construction activities
  • Sponsorship is not available for this role
  • Relocation is not available for this role

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. In the Microsoft Frontier Company Engineering team, you won’t just build software; you’ll deliver real outcomes for some of the world’s most complex organizations.

As a Principal Technical Program Manager, you will embed with strategic customers to lead complex technical programs, owning the full customer journey from problem definition through delivery and driving measurable business outcomes. You’ll work in small, multidisciplinary crews alongside engineers, data scientists, and designers, operating with high autonomy to turn ambiguous problems into shipped solutions.

Our work is powered by AI, applying the mindset and tooling across the entire development lifecycle to move from idea to production in days while maintaining the highest standards of security, quality, and trust.

This role offers the opportunity to:

  • Lead complex technical programs from problem definition through to delivered outcomes

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees, we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities
  • Embed with strategic customers to lead complex technical programs with high autonomy, aligning business needs with engineering solutions across AI, cloud, and data. Take ownership of the customer journey end-to-end, from problem definition through co-engineering delivery to measurable business outcomes.

Additional or Preferred Qualifications (PQs)

title: HPEFS Sr. Process Engineer
description:
HPEFS Sr. Process Engineer

This role has been designed as ‘’Onsite’ with an expectation that you will primarily work from an HPE office.

Who We Are:

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world. Our culture thrives on finding new and better ways to accelerate what’s next. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good. If you are looking to stretch and grow your career our culture will embrace you. Open up opportunities with HPE.

Job Description:

We are seeking an HPEFS Sr. Process Engineer to support our Spring, TX or Berkeley Heights, NJ on a hybrid schedule.

About the Role

HPE Financial Services within HPE is seeking a highly experienced individual contributor Process Engineer who serves as an expert in driving process excellence across complex, cross-functional environments.

The primary objective is to identify, design, and implement sustainable process improvements that deliver measurable business value.

The role is grounded in strong process engineering fundamentals, while leveraging automation, analytics, and AI as accelerators to enhance speed, insight, and scalability across projects. You will work closely with global business stakeholders to solve complex process challenges, define best practices, and embed continuous improvement into the organizational culture.

Role Overview

  • Subject matter expert in process engineering concepts, solving complex business issues through structured methodologies.
  • Leads high-impact, cross-functional process improvement initiatives requiring deep evaluation of business operations
  • Continuously contributes towards improving process engineering frameworks, governance, and standards.
  • Provides guidance and mentorship to build organizational capability in process excellence.

Responsibilities

Process Improvement & Value Delivery

  • Leads end-to-end process improvement initiatives from discovery through value realization while leveraging the process engineering framework and templates
  • Provide DMAIC based approach to projects to drive business value for the company, lead focused, collaborative, cross-functional deep-dive workshops for high priority initiatives and bring process and data driven focused approach to support the organization's goals
  • Partner with business stakeholders to identify inefficiencies, root causes, and improvement opportunities across processes while risk ratings the failure modes
  • Clearly able to corelate and map multiple tracks of process engineering work for synergies and lineage
  • Translate process insights into clear, actionable recommendations (to-be) and business cases focused on measurable outcomes
  • Drive a value-first mindset, ensuring all process improvements are linked to tangible business impact.
  • Champions the value realization framework to ensure measurable outcomes are part of the process engineering outcomes

Process Engineering & Methodology

  • Apply Lean Six Sigma, Design Thinking, and Agile methods to analyze, redesign, and optimize processes.
  • Conduct structured process assessments, including process mapping (L1- L4), root cause analysis, and waste identification applying FMEA and 5 Why concepts as applicable
  • Continuously contributes towards process standards, frameworks, and governance mechanisms for consistent execution.
  • Design and embed controls and monitoring mechanisms to ensure sustainability of improvements.
  • Leverage automations & AI to optimize the process improvement projects while reducing the turnaround times of process engineering engagements
  • Well versed with using analytics and process mining tools to support a data driven approach
  • Change management – Drive sustainable change through the organization through collaboration and cross function work. Establish process, procedures to ensure sustainability of project results

Stakeholder Engagement & Influence

  • Proactive engagement, communications with cross-functional stakeholders across business units to align on process improvement priorities, deliverables and execution plans.
  • Influence business leaders to adopt process-led thinking and continuous improvement practices.
  • Communicate complex process issues in a clear, business-focused manner.

Capability Building

  • Mentor junior team members and peers contribute to building a strong process engineering capability across the organization.
  • Provide Yellow belt and Green belt training to potential candidates and upon request from the business
  • Contribute to the evolution of process engineering practices and continuous improvement culture.
  • Share knowledge, best practices, and learnings to drive consistency and maturity in process excellence.

Experience & Qualifications

  • 7–8 years of hands-on process engineering experience with a strong track record of delivering measurable business impact — ideally in a global, matrixed organization where speed-to-value and stakeholder influence are critical success factors.
  • Lean Six Sigma Green Belt (required) or Black Belt (strongly preferred), with demonstrated ability to apply Design Thinking and Agile methodologies alongside traditional process improvement tools
  • Proficiency with statistical techniques, flow charting, business analysis and experience in finance, banking, leasing and customer success / services environment in technology industry
  • Experience using AI and automation as accelerators within improvement projects is essential.
  • Practical experience with at least one process mining platform, with the ability to independently extract, interpret, and act on process intelligence data.
  • Strong business acumen and stakeholder engagement skills — able to quickly build credibility with senior leaders, translate process complexity into business impact narratives, and influence decision-making without relying solely on data or formal authority.
  • Based in or able to commute to Spring, TX or Berkeley Heights, NJ at least 3 days per week
  • Comfortable working across global time zones and collaborating with international teams and customers as part of a globally distributed organization
  • Ability to work independently and guide complex initiatives with minimal supervision.
  • Strong communication skills to manage cross-functional teams and stakeholders across the globe

What We Can Offer You:

Health & Wellbeing

We strive to provide our team members and their loved ones with a comprehensive suite of benefits that supports their physical, financial and emotional wellbeing.

Personal & Professional Development

We also invest in your career because the better you are, the better we all are. We have specific programs catered to helping you reach any career goals you have — whether you want to become a knowledge expert in your field or apply your skills to another division.

Unconditional Inclusion

We are unconditionally inclusive in the way we work and celebrate individual uniqueness. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good.

Let's Stay Connected:

Follow @HPECareers on Instagram to see the latest on people, culture and tech at HPE.

title: CT Imaging Technologist, PRN
description:
Cabinet Peaks Medical Center is looking for a CT Imaging Technologist to join our Imaging Department!

Under the supervision of the Imaging Manager and under the general direction of the Imaging Medical Director, performs quality and complete imaging procedures to assist in a diagnosis of disease and injuries. The Imaging Technologist works effectively with patients and patients' families and maintains a cooperative relationship with interdepartmental personnel. The Technologist is responsible for providing patient education, quality patient care, and will meet all regulatory compliance. This is not a comprehensive job description, and other duties or responsibilities may be assigned as needed.


Major Job Duties & Responsibilities

Produces quality exams within assigned modalities and assigned areas, including portable and C-Arm applications, X-Ray, DXA, CT, and fluoroscopic procedures. Applies principles of radiation protection, choice of protocol, knowledge of anatomy and pathology.

Maintains patient records and files, as appropriate. Properly navigates PACS. Provides accurate history, completed forms, and appropriate documentation of each exam performed.

Actively participates in departmental quality assurance program including preventative maintenance and other quality measures.

Practices patient safety including correct patient identification, safe transfers, radiation safety, standard precautions, infection control, fall prevention, and other patient safety measures.

Follows appropriate rules of punctuality, shift rotation, and modality coverage.

Performs other duties as requested by Manager.

Follows departmental policies and procedures.

Prepares and administers contrast media through IV or other routes.

Provides instruction and supervision to radiologic technologist students who are fulfilling their clinical requirements at CPMC.

Provides administrative duties, as needed, in connection with the front desk responsibilities of the department – alongside or in the absence of the receptionist.

Maintains competency in C.T.


Skills, Knowledge & Abilities

Pursues continuing education.

In absence of Manager, the Technologist is able to assume responsibilities of the department.

Able to work well in situations of stress.

Practices professional interpersonal communication.

Must be willing and able to take call.

Must be willing to learn other imaging modalities as Manager and Medical Director see fit.

Able and willing to perform other duties as assigned.


Schedule

Schedule will be based on the needs of the department and shifts will vary.

This includes standard daytime hours, nighttime hours, weekend shifts and night call shifts.


Educational Requirements

Technologist must be a HS graduate or equivalent and have completed an accredited program in radiologic technology.

Technologist must be registered as a radiologic technologist through ARRT.

title: Senior Environmental Planner - Transmission
description:
AECOM has an exciting opportunity for a Senior Environmental Planner - Transmission to join our Environmental Planning and Permitting (EPP) team in the Midwest region.

This hybrid role can be based out of AECOM's Indianapolis, Chicago, Milwaukee, Columbus, Minneapolis, St. Louis, Kansas City, or Detroit offices. Consideration will also be given for all locations in the Upper Midwest.

Our EPP team serves numerous private industry and public utility energy clients, on a variety of energy projects including transmission, grid modernization, and renewable energy developments. In this role you will lead project teams and work with our environmental planning practitioners and technical subject matter experts to prepare environmental documents, with a particular focus on supporting permitting and entitlement work for our growing line of work with energy developers and utilities. Projects range from regional transmission programs and grid modernization efforts to large-scale renewable energy developments and complex, multi-jurisdictional permitting efforts.

This role would involve serving as a seller-doer, responsible for developing and maintaining client relationships, leading pursuits and project teams, and expanding AECOM's energy permitting and environmental planning portfolio across the Midwest and supporting strategic growth initiatives throughout the U.S.

The responsibilities of this role would include, but are not limited to:

  • Lead environmental planning and compliance efforts for energy infrastructure projects, and coordination and filings with state utility regulatory agencies and public service commissions to support transmission siting, routing, permitting, and certificate approval processes across Midwest jurisdictions, especially within MISO, PJM, and SPP regions. Will include preparation of technical studies and NEPA documentation.
  • Manage early-stage due diligence efforts for siting energy projects and associated infrastructure.
  • Provide project management on mid- to large-sized projects, including developing and tracking project schedules, budgets, invoicing, and coordination with clients, technical staff and subconsultants.
  • Work on environmental documents and entitlements related to high-profile infrastructure projects, with particular emphasis on energy sector projects.
  • Support projects across the Midwest and other U.S. markets by leveraging AECOM's national technical and project delivery platform.
  • Contribute to marketing and business development, preparation of proposals, and formulating proposal cost estimates as a seller-doer.
  • Mentor and develop junior and mid-level staff by reviewing work products, providing technical guidance, and supporting career development.

About AECOM’s Environment Business Line
Join AECOM to be part of an expert global team who is connected through a well-developed, worldwide, internal technical practice network through which you can learn from and brainstorm with the best in the world. AECOM is an industry-leading, world class environmental firm, and we want you to succeed within it. We respect and encourage your own pathway to excellence via our Freedom to Grow initiative.

AECOM is known for our award-winning technical excellence, leading-edge science and innovative project delivery. We provide sustainable solutions for some of the world’s most challenging issues. Our global clients and their projects span a variety of market sectors and geographies and require innovative technical solutions to solve wide-ranging environmental problems.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in environmental planning, environmental science, geography, natural resources, engineering, or a related field.
  • 6 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education in electric transmission and renewable energy (e.g., solar, wind, energy storage) through preparing state utility permitting applications, routing and siting analysis, critical issues analysis, land use entitlement applications and/or overseeing multi-disciplinary technical teams for resource technical studies and permitting.
  • Ability to travel for agency/client meetings, as needed.
  • A valid U.S Driver's license is required for this role.
  • Due to the nature of this work, U.S. Citizenship is required.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 10+ years successfully managing permitting and preparing state utility commission and related documentation, strong understanding of current state and federal regulations and guidance.
  • Electric transmission and renewable energy (e.g., solar, wind, energy storage) experience through preparing state utility commissions documents, routing and siting analysis, critical issues analysis, land use entitlement applications and/or overseeing multi-disciplinary technical teams for resource technical studies and permitting, as well as NEPA documentation.
  • Advanced experience leading complex transmission and renewable energy permitting programs, including strategic permitting, agency negotiation, and multi-state routing effort
  • Experience leading transmission permitting, routing, and certificate proceedings before state utility commissions and public service commissions within the Midwest or other U.S. jurisdictions. Experience supporting regulatory hearings or expert witness testimony is a plus.
  • Experience supporting client development, proposal preparation, and/or business development pursuits.
  • Experience managing environmental planning or permitting projects, including scope, schedule, budget, and client communications.
  • Project management experience on environmental planning projects, including client interaction, schedule and budget controls, and invoicing.
  • Demonstrated leadership in proposal development and successful pursuit of competitive bids.
  • Experience working in a fast-paced consulting environment, managing and mentoring staff.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

title: Counsellor, Crisis Call Diversion
company: CMHA Thames Valley Addiction and Mental Health Services
description:
Counsellor, Crisis Call Diversion
Direct Service - (OPSEU)
Part-Time, Contract (Ending: December 31, 2027)
London, Ontario (London Zone)
This posting is the result of an upcoming vacancy
- Application Deadline: August 12, 2026 -


We believe when individuals in our community experience an urgent mental health or addictions crisis, they deserve a response that is person-centred and supportive, while focusing on personal dignity and wellbeing.

The Crisis Call Diversion (CCD) program is a partnership with the London Police Service (LPS). Staff are positioned at the London Police Service Communications Centre to work with call takers and dispatchers to divert non-imminent risk mental health calls away from a police response and towards a more appropriate mental health response.

Crisis Call Diversion staff will support individuals accessing emergency services through the London Police Services (LPS) by providing a psychosocial response in order to promote crisis resolution and empowerment for the individual. Crisis Call Diversion staff will also work collaboratively with individuals to assess and identify their needs and link them to appropriate supports in the community.

Consider revitalizing your career and making a difference in your community by joining our team!

WHAT WE'RE OFFERING:

  • What you'll be making - Starting rate for this role is $27.14 per hour (Level 1 – Direct Service), with a wage differential, based on regulation ($30.01 per hour for Level 1 – Direct Service, Regulated):
    1. Successful candidates who are registered with one of the designated professional colleges (e.g. OCSWSSW, CNO, COTO, CRPO, CPSO, or CPO) will receive the wage differential for regulation
    2. Successful external applicants will start at Level 1, with grid progression based on seniority up to Level 8 ($34.41 per hour for non-regulated, and $37.26 per hour for regulated); for internal applicants, grid level placement will occur as per the Collective Agreement
  • When you'll work - 36 hours bi-weekly; Nights (including weekends); paid 30-minute meal break
  • Your pension plan –Immediately eligible for optional enrollment in the Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan (HOOPP)
  • What your benefits will be – 9% in lieu of benefits

HOW YOU WILL BE MAKING A DIFFERENCE:

Direct Service:

  • Complete phone mental health and addiction assessments based on theory of crisis management including rapid response to identify:
    • the impact of psychiatric symptoms on functioning,
    • risk factors related to safety of client and others,
    • opportunities for de-escalation and stabilization.
  • Establish a therapeutic relationship to maximize the benefits of engagement with the individual.
  • Provide short-term follow-up and support.
  • Coordinate and facilitate referrals to internal and external services and supports.
  • Advocate as necessary, in order to facilitate access to services and supports with the objective of remediating the immediate crisis situation.
  • Engage and work collaboratively with emergency services when it is determined that additional intervention is required.
  • Assess barriers to successful community living (e.g. treatment options, transportation, finances, etc.).
  • Obtain information, as needed, from other relevant sources.
  • Interact and provide support and assessment in a non-judgmental fashion and provide care that demonstrates sensitivity to individual diversity (e.g. culture, race, age, sexual orientation, gender, beliefs and values, etc.).
  • Support the individual in developing skills for self-advocacy to learn new behaviours and develop coping skills fostering healthy interdependence through limit setting.
  • Provide health teaching and information regarding coping techniques and strategies, (e.g. grounding, breathing techniques, self-care, nutrition, sleep hygiene, techniques to enhance overall well-being, etc.).
Crisis Intervention:
  • Provide short-term, psychotherapeutic intervention to assist individuals in gaining insight and improving coping skills within the framework of the crisis model.
  • Perform in a calm, competent and efficient manner in an emergency situation acknowledging the individual’s need for empathy, privacy and dignity.
  • Utilize harm reduction principles to identify, reduce and remove risk factors.
Crisis Follow-Up:
  • Refer individuals for additional assessments as is determined to be necessary and / or appropriate under the circumstances.
  • Assist the individual to identify and connect with personal / natural supports.
  • Provide follow-up support via the phone and / or e-mail to provide resources, and act as a tool for successful safety planning and prevention of a future crisis.
Coordination and Advocacy:
  • Demonstrate a knowledge of community resources and its place within the mental health and addiction care system.
  • Assist in building positive working relationships across the service system including CMHA, emergency service partners (i.e. police) and other social or health care providers.
  • Participate in committees, working groups or situation tables as needed to promote effective service coordination and collaboration.
  • Participate in public education and advocacy and provide public demonstrations when required.
  • When appropriate, act as liaison with caregivers and / or service and support providers who are involved with the individual to facilitate a coordinated approach to service provision.
24/7 Reach Out Addiction and Mental Health Crisis Line responsibilities:
  • All Crisis Clinicians are to provide support to individuals through Reach Out.
  • Provide crisis intervention services and supports on Reach Out via phone, text and web chat.
  • Respond to voicemails from Reach Out.
  • Establish a therapeutic relationship with individuals accessing Reach Out, and work with individuals to address their immediate concerns.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO APPLY:

Police Vulnerable Sector Check Requirements
Successful candidates must have a Police Vulnerable Sector Check completed in the last six months. Interested applicants who reside in the City of London and are in need of a Police Vulnerable Sector Check (PVSC) are encouraged to apply for one as soon as possible as PVSCs in the City of London are currently taking approximately 2 weeks to be processed and offers of employment cannot be made without receipt of a PVSC.

We require the following qualifications:

  • Degree or diploma in a mental health or addictions related field or a minimum of 3 years of experience in a direct-service role and some post-secondary education in a mental health or addictions related field (primary proof of credentials will be required during the hiring process i.e. original degree/diploma or official transcript)
  • Current, satisfactory Police Vulnerable Sector Check (PVSC)
  • Demonstrated ability to attend work regularly

We prefer the following qualifications:

  • Training in crisis intervention and crisis resolution, including ASIST training program.
  • First Aid & CPR, WHMIS Training
  • Valid Driver’s License
  • Access to a vehicle for personal transportation
  • Extensive knowledge of community resources, service and support programs, as well as barriers participants face in accessing supports.
  • Working knowledge of a variety of treatment, intervention, and support strategies to support mental health.
  • Minimum of 3-5 years experience working in mental health, including a minimum of 2 years experience working in crisis intervention.
  • Experience with, and detailed knowledge of, mild, moderate and serious mental illnesses.
  • Experience working in a community-based setting, preferably with an established network of service and support resources.
  • Ability to assess level of risk with regards to clients
  • Proficiency in the areas of crisis intervention, crisis resolution, and community support.
  • Strong written, notetaking and verbal communication skills.
  • Bilingual both official languages, preferred; préférence sera accordée aux candidats qui sont compétents dans les deux langues officielles du Canada

INTERNAL APPLICANTS: To be considered as an internal applicant, current staff members are reminded to apply using their @cmhatv.ca or @slwar.ca email address.

Get your application in by – August 12, 2026

Our recruitment process allows us to learn about your previous work experience, your qualifications and your commitment to fulfilling our vision. While we appreciate the interest of all applicants, only those individuals being considered for a position will be personally contacted by someone from the interview team.

We welcome and encourage applications from all members of our community including persons of any gender, gender identity, gender expression, or sexual orientation, persons with disabilities, Indigenous persons, and members of visible minorities. If you require accommodations related to a disability at any point during the recruitment process, please contact Human.Resources@cmhatv.ca

title: Immediate Care Center Patient Flow Coordinator RN Part time
description:
The Patient Flow Coordinator, RN (PFC, RN) reflects the mission, vision, and values of Northwestern Medicine, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards. The PFC, RN is a skilled professional nurse with competence in a specialized area of nursing. Works cooperatively and communicates effectively within a framework to actively promote holistic care for patients. Demonstrates self-direction and initiative in the role of nurse clinician, educator, and consultant. Provides direct patient care and/or consultation using in-depth clinical knowledge and skills in area of expertise. Promotes customer service and communication between the healthcare team and patient. The Patient Flow Coordinator should work autonomously within the guidelines set by ICC medical leadership and efficiently in a fast-paced environment. The Patient Flow Coordinator role is performed from within designated Northwestern Medicine ICC locations and requires in-clinic orientation. This position will work 12-hour shifts and include weekend and holiday requirements.

Responsibilities:

  • Maintain a safe and clean work environment. Ensure compliance with OSHA regulations. Report deficiencies to supervisor immediately. Assist in rectifying deficiencies as requested. Assume responsibility for and supervision of the appropriate care of medical equipment.
  • For each patient, perform a comprehensive assessment of the chief complaint and patient needs utilizing the nursing process. Based on findings, seek solutions and offer opinions to physicians and other health care providers. Document all nursing assessments in the patient's medical record. Ensure that all documentation is clear, complete and legible. Maintain patient confidentiality at all times. Understand and uphold the protocols and procedures for release of patient medical information.
  • Demonstrate clinical competency and independently perform routine nursing duties including phlebotomy, medication administration, measurement of vital signs, preparation of lab specimens, etc.
  • Interpret and define abnormalities detected in tests and procedures, then take appropriate remedial action. Document all interventions in the patient medical record as appropriate.
  • Communicate and collaborate with other clinical and administrative departments in order to coordinate appropriate patient care, as needed.
  • Communicate with outside agencies or facilities as appropriate.
  • Triage and prioritize incoming telephone calls and results using clinical assessment skills and service standards. Communicate results/plan of care with patients by phone or MyChart per department procedure. Document all assessments in the patient medical record as appropriate.
  • Manage urgent/emergent medical situations as appropriate and in accordance with the organization's protocols for medical emergencies and cardiac arrests. Obtain and/or operate emergency equipment according to relevant standards.
  • Serve as a resource for staff and physicians for daily problem solving and decision-making. Maintain a consistent alertness to patient care needs and take a proactive approach to address/resolve issues. Delegate appropriate tasks according to Illinois law and organizational protocols.
  • Comply with all existing policies and procedures related to patient care. Make recommendations to management regarding new policies and procedures that may improve the patient experience. Assure that new policies and procedures are implemented in a timely manner.
  • Initiate and coordinate patient education. Ensure that patients understand educational materials and can exhibit return demonstration when pertinent.
  • Serve as a resource and role model for team members by providing feedback and assisting with clinical education.
  • Other duties as assigned

BEHAVIORAL EXPECTATIONS

  • Ability to function independently and as part of the ICC team
  • Excellent at multitasking in a fast-paced environment
  • Excellent critical thinking and high tolerance for ambiguity
  • Responds effectively to changes in ICC workflow due to volume, use of new technology, staffing, volume control, or closures.

Required:

  • BSN
  • Current Registered Nurse License issued by State of Illinois
  • BLS certification
  • Minimum two years of RN experience

Preferred:

  • Minimum of three years of emergency department or urgent care setting
  • National certification in specialty area such as CEN, TCRN, Ambulatory Care, or others
  • Proficient with Epic electronic charting system

title: Cyber Intelligence Vice President -Blockchain
description:
Join a team where your expertise in blockchain security and threat intelligence will directly protect one of the world's most sophisticated financial institutions. At JPMorganChase, you will have the opportunity to work at the forefront of digital asset security, leveraging cutting-edge tools and intelligence-driven methodologies to defend institutional blockchain infrastructure. This role offers unparalleled exposure to emerging on-chain threats, cross-functional collaboration, and the chance to shape the future of cybersecurity in financial services.

As a Blockchain Intelligence Vice President at JPMorganChase within Cybersecurity & Tech Controls, you will contribute significantly to safeguarding the organization's digital assets and infrastructure by proactively identifying, tracking, detecting, assessing, and responding to threats, vulnerabilities, and security incidents. You will regularly collaborate with cross-functional teams to develop a coordinated approach to security, ensuring the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of sensitive data and systems. You will apply advanced analytical, technical, and problem-solving skills to enable operational excellence and implement innovative solutions to address complex security challenges. By staying current with industry best practices, policies, and procedures, you will contribute to maintaining a secure digital environment and driving continuous improvement in the firm.

Embrace the challenge of securing institutional blockchain infrastructure at scale, delivering intelligence-driven operational excellence across on-chain monitoring operations, and implementing cutting-edge detection capabilities for smart contract and digital asset security.

Job responsibilities

  • Execute and influence the design of comprehensive security and threat intelligence strategies, policies, and procedures to enhance threat detection capabilities and protect the organization's digital assets, smart contracts, and blockchain infrastructure from cybersecurity threats
  • Proactively monitor and analyze complex on-chain and off-chain data and systems to identify indicators of vulnerabilities and compromises, utilizing advanced tools and techniques to detect anomalies and contribute to the development of strategies for security investigation, threat mitigation, and incident response
  • Produce actionable threat intelligence products including indicator of compromise development, exploit analysis reports, and threat actor tracking to inform detection engineering and security operations.
  • Uses enterprise-authorized AI capabilities within the work environment to accelerate threat intelligence synthesis and prioritization, validating outputs and handling data according to sensitivity and security requirements.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure a coordinated approach to blockchain and enterprise security, sharing threat intelligence insights, and promoting best practices across the organization
  • Evaluate and enhance the organization's security posture by staying current with industry trends, emerging on-chain threats, threat actor tactics, techniques, and procedures, and regulatory requirements, driving innovation and process improvements.
  • Drives reuse-first adoption of AI-assisted workflows to improve threat hunting and detection engineering productivity, ensuring outputs are validated and aligned to security expectations.
  • Partner with detection engineering teams to translate intelligence findings into scalable, automated detection rules and monitoring frameworks
  • Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of incident response playbooks specific to blockchain and digital asset threat scenarios

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Formal training or certification on cyber intelligence concepts and 5+ years applied experience.
  • Demonstrated expertise in multiple security domains, including network security, malware analysis, threat hunting, threat intelligence production, and security architecture and design, with proficiency in using Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) tools and advanced analytics techniques
  • Advanced knowledge of network and infrastructure configuration and security, including experience in designing and implementing security solutions for on-premises, cloud, or hybrid environments.
  • Demonstrated experience using enterprise-authorized AI capabilities within the work environment to support threat intelligence, detection engineering, and security research workflows with strong validation habits and awareness of data sensitivity.
  • Ability to review and validate AI-assisted intelligence findings and detection recommendations before implementation, escalating when uncertain and following security and data handling requirements.
  • Proven ability to analyze complex on-chain and off-chain data to identify threat indicators, anomalies, and patterns indicative of malicious activity
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to produce clear, concise, and actionable intelligence reports for both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Experience working in cross-functional environments, coordinating with security operations, engineering, and risk teams to drive coordinated threat response

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Familiarity with broader blockchain security concepts such as consensus mechanisms, smart contract vulnerability classes, blockchain threat actor landscape, and multi-chain monitoring approaches
  • Experience with digital asset platforms, decentralized finance protocols, or blockchain forensics tooling
  • Knowledge of regulatory frameworks and compliance requirements relevant to digital assets and financial services cybersecurity
  • Relevant industry certifications such as Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), GIAC Cyber Threat Intelligence (GCTI), or equivalent

MINIMUM AND/OR PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

EDUCATION

  • College degree; degrees in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Technical, Business, or related fields preferred. MBA a plus.

EXPERIENCE

  • Experience with complex data analysis, data strategy, data modeling, data migrations, data integration, and ETL processes across enterprise environments.

  • Experience working directly with enterprise clients and collaborating across sales, delivery, and customer success teams.

SKILL REQUIREMENTS
